title: Association between biological age acceleration and the risk of aortic valve stenosis: An observational epidemiologic and Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Yiqi Zheng; Xinghao Xu; Ruijie Li; Zhenyu Xiong; Han Wen; Yue Guo; Menghui Liu; Huimin Zhou; Xingfeng Xu; Shaozhao Zhang; Rihua Huang; Zezhi Ke; Zihao Huang; Jiayuan Zhang; Xiaodong Zhuang; Xinxue Liao
journal: The journal of nutrition, health & aging
abstract:
Biological age acceleration (BAA) is thought to be a major risk factor for age-related diseases, but its role in aortic valve stenosis (AVS) remains uncertain. We aimed to assess the associations between biological aging and the risk of AVS.
This study involved 4526 participants from the Real-world Data of Cardiometabolic Protection (RED-CARPET) study and 5114 participants from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) study. BAA was assessed using clinical biomarkers through the Klemera-Doubal method (KDM) and the PhenoAge algorithm. We employed multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) regression to examine the association between BAA and AVS risk. Additionally, Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was conducted to assess causality.
In the RED-CARPET cohort of 4526 participants (mean age 60.93 years, 33.5% female), 113 AVS events were recorded. In the ARIC cohort of 5114 participants (mean age 51.94 years, 56.4% female, 82.3% White), there were 266 AVS events. After fully adjusting for confounding variables, each standard deviation increase in BAA was significantly associated with elevated AVS risk (RED-CARPET: KDM-BA acceleration: OR 1.29, 95% CI 1.07-1.55; PhenoAge acceleration: OR 1.48, 95% CI 1.24-1.77; ARIC: KDM-BA acceleration: OR 1.42, 95% CI 1.24-1.63; PhenoAge acceleration: OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.11-1.51). The RCS regression model revealed significant linear relationships between BAA and the risk of AVS in both cohorts. MR analysis suggested a potential causal relationship between KDM-BA acceleration and AVS risk (OR 1.38, 95% CI 1.21-1.57).
BAA, as derived from clinical biomarkers, is independently associated with an increased risk of AVS. This finding suggests that BAA, as a composite indicator of systemic biological aging, may complement traditional risk factors in the early identification of high-risk populations for AVS, and offer the possibility of early intervention for prevention.

title: Ultra-high-pitch photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) versus ultra-high-pitch dual-source computed tomography (DSCT) for coronary artery disease evaluation in transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) patients.
authors: Ines Mecking; Marc von der Stück; Eric Corban; Michael Frick; Jörg Schröder; Roman Iwa; Christiane K Kuhl; Timm Dirrichs
abstract:
To compare radiation dose and image quality of coronary artery reconstructions obtained from non-coronary-dedicated transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) planning CT scans using ultra-high-pitch photon-counting CT (PCCT) and ultra-high-pitch energy-integrating detector dual-source CT (EID-DSCT; hereafter referred to as DSCT), including assessment of the feasibility of coronary artery evaluation according to the Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS).
Retrospective study on consecutive patients with aortic valve stenosis (AS) undergoing contrast-enhanced TAVI planning CT, either PCCT or DSCT between August 2021 and June 2023. CT dose index (CTDI) and dose length product (DLP) were used to calculate the effective radiation dose (eRD). Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) were calculated using standardized region-of-interest (ROI) analysis. Coronary arteries were evaluated by three independent radiologists using 5-point Likert scales followed by a classification according to the CAD-RADS system.
187 patients (83 female, median age 82, IQR: 76-84) underwent 190 CT-examinations, 103 PCCT (54.2%) and 87 (45.8%) DSCT. Three patients underwent both PCCT and DSCT for clinical reasons. Mean CTDI and DLP were significantly lower in PCCT compared to DSCT (21.9 vs. 52.8 and 607.9 vs. 906.8, respectively; both p < 0.001), with a correspondingly lower mean effective radiation dose (eRD) in PCCT compared to DSCT (10.3 ± 5.4 mSv vs. 15.4 ± 5.6 mSv, p < 0.001). While both SNR and CNR were lower in PCCT than in DSCT (SNR: 35.28 ± 11.63 in PCCT vs. 45.6 ± 16.3 in DSCT, p < 0.001; CNR: 49.25 ± 13.31 in PCCT vs. 57.42 v ± 22.55 in DSCT, p = 0.004), PCCT outperformed DSCT in every one of the eleven visual image categories. Overall image quality was rated as good or excellent in 71.8% (74/103) of PCCT vs. 19.5% (17/87) of DSCT scans. Coronary reconstructions were rated as good or excellent in 72.8% (75/103) of PCCT vs. 20.7% of DSCT datasets. CAD-RADS [1-5] rating was possible in 68.9% (71/103) of PCCT vs. 39.1% (34/87) of DSCT datasets.
Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) allows for significantly improved assessability of the coronary arteries in TAVI planning CT compared with dual-source CT (DSCT), while achieving a substantially lower radiation dose.

title: Association between early vein graft failure and long-term major adverse cardiovascular events following off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting: an exploratory retrospective cohort study.
authors: Zhaoxi Qi; Yunpeng Zhu; Xiaofeng Ye; Zhe Wang; Sigrid E Sandner; Yi Yang; Qiang Zhao
abstract:
Early vein graft failure (VGF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is far from rare and often clinically silent. While mid-to-late graft failure is established to predict adverse clinical events, the long-term prognostic impact of predischarge early VGF remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate the association between early VGF and 10-year clinical outcomes following off-pump CABG.
In this exploratory retrospective cohort study, adult patients undergoing elective isolated off-pump CABG using vein grafts with early postoperative coronary computed tomography angiography between July 2014 and December 2015 were consecutively included. Baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative data were collected from electronic medical records. VGF was defined as Fitzgibbon grade B (≥50% stenosis) or O (occlusion). Patients were stratified into the early VGF group (with at least one failed vein graft) and non-early VGF group (without failed vein grafts). Clinical follow-up was conducted through routine outpatient visits or standardized telephone interviews in accordance with institutional protocol. Primary outcomes included 10-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE, composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or revascularization) and its individual components. Secondary outcomes included perioperative myocardial injury and perioperative myocardial infarction (PMI). Propensity score overlap weighting was applied to adjust for baseline confounders. Exploratory post-hoc landmark and piecewise Cox analyses were performed to address non-proportional hazards.
A total of 233 patients were included in the analyses (mean age 64.3±7.5 years; 18.4% female). Among them, early VGF was identified in 33 (14.2%) patients and 41 (5.9%) vein grafts. Early VGF numerically increased the risk of perioperative myocardial injury [45.5% vs. 30.5%, odds ratio (OR) 1.90, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.89-4.01; P=0.09] and PMI (12.1% vs. 6.0%, OR 2.16, 95% CI: 0.57-6.69; P=0.21), though without statistical significance. Over a median follow-up of 9.6 years, there was no statistically significant difference in 10-year MACE between the two groups [early VGF 51.5% vs. non-early VGF 48.2%; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 1.31, 95% CI: 0.76-2.24; P=0.33]. In exploratory landmark analyses addressing non-proportional hazards (P=0.03), early VGF was associated with a higher risk of MACE within the first 2 years post-surgery (aHR 2.18, 95% CI: 1.14-4.17; P=0.02), which attenuated beyond the 2-year landmark (aHR 0.56, 95% CI: 0.22-1.46; P=0.24). Additionally, early VGF was associated with a higher risk of repeat revascularization (18.2% vs. 7.7%; aHR 3.06, 95% CI: 1.13-8.31; P=0.03).
Predischarge early VGF was not significantly associated with the overall 10-year risk of MACE following off-pump CABG. Exploratory findings regarding early risk clustering within 2 years and an increased risk of repeat revascularization remain hypothesis-generating. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate these observations.

title: Comparative validation of standard screening tools and an exploratory model for detecting obstructive sleep apnea in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
authors: Shahid Karim; Balambika S Iyyappan; Sair Tabraiz; Aishwarya Rajendran; Anwar Chahal; Jeffrey B Geske; Alanna M Chamberlain; Virend K Somers
abstract:
Despite representing a highly prevalent comorbidity, standard screening tools for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) lack validation in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) population. We sought to prospectively evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of three widely used screening tools against gold-standard polysomnography in an HCM cohort and to explore the potential for a tailored predictive model.
In this prospective cohort study, patients with HCM completed the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), Berlin (BQ) and STOP-Bang questionnaires before undergoing inpatient overnight polysomnography.
Of 159 participants (median age 60; 64% male), 90 (57%) had OSA (46% mild, 26% moderate, 28% severe). Standard tools yielded modest performance: STOP-Bang [AUC 0.59 (0.50-0.68), sensitivity 77% (68-86), specificity 40% (28-52)]; ESS [AUC 0.58 (0.49-0.67), sensitivity 24% (15-33), specificity 92% (86-98)]; and Berlin [AUC 0.62 (0.53-0.71), sensitivity 65% (55-75), specificity 57% (45-69)]. In contrast, an exploratory model incorporating age, BMI, and waist-hip ratio showed promising preliminary results [AUC 0.82 (0.74-0.88), sensitivity 60% (48-72), specificity 84% (75-91)].
This study underscores the high prevalence of OSA in patients with HCM and demonstrates that standard screening tools developed for the general population perform poorly in this cohort, complicating clinical triage when polysomnography is delayed. While the derived exploratory model may represent an improvement in risk stratification, these findings require extensive external validation. Targeted screening strategies tailored to the unique pathophysiology of HCM remain necessary to improve OSA identification and management in this high-risk population.

title: Phase 4 Atrioventricular Block Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Unmasking Latent Conduction Disease.
authors: Shivani Reddy; Ariane T Lemieux; Alan Donsky; Manish Assar; Robert C Stoler
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) carries up to a 15% risk of complete heart block (CHB) within 30 days, but the mechanisms driving recurrent heart block after the apparent initial conduction system recovery post-TAVR remain incompletely understood. Phase 4 atrioventricular block, a pause-dependent phenomenon occurring when supraventricular or ventricular impulses encounter diseased His-Purkinje fibers during diastolic depolarization, may contribute to post-TAVR conduction disturbances. We present an instructive case of a 71-year-old woman with severe aortic valve stenosis who developed CHB in the setting of phase 4 atrioventricular block following TAVR. Despite recovering sinus rhythm with 1:1 atrioventricular conduction within 12 hours post-procedure, she experienced recurrent ventricular standstill upon temporary pacemaker removal, ultimately requiring permanent pacemaker implantation. This case illustrates the multiple mechanisms and temporal patterns of post-TAVR conduction system disorders, the potential unreliability of early apparent conduction recovery as a predictor of durable atrioventricular conduction, and the necessity for careful and more prolonged patient monitoring before and after temporary pacemaker removal.

title: Surgical outcomes of infective endocarditis in children and adults with congenital heart disease.
authors: Thibault Schaeffer; Kenan Alaham; Doris Kienmoser; Andrea Amici; Jonas Palm; Teresa Lemmen; Christina Ruda; Nicole Piber; Muneaki Matsubara; Paul Philipp Heinisch; Alfred Hager; Peter Ewert; Jürgen Hörer; Masamichi Ono
journal: The Journal of thoracic and cardiovascular surgery
abstract:
Reports describing surgery for infective endocarditis (IE) in children and adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) are limited. This study aimed to determine the patient characteristics, preoperative conditions, surgical outcomes, and risk factors in this cohort.
All children and adults with CHD who underwent surgical treatment for IE between 2001 and 2024 were reviewed. Patient characteristics and surgical procedures were evaluated; survival, recurrent IE, and risk factors were analyzed.
A total of 96 patients underwent surgical treatment for IE, including 52 children and 44 adults with CHD. Underlying CHD included ventricular septal defect in 31 patients, aortic stenosis/insufficiency in 26, and tetralogy of Fallot in 14. The most frequently infected lesion was the aortic valve in 40 patients, and the most frequently detected organism was Staphylococcus species in 34 patients. Vegetation was observed in 65 patients. Median age at surgery was 17.2 (IQR: 11.7-29.4) years. In-hospital mortality was 6.3%, and survival at 5, 10, and 20 years was 90.6, 88.1, and 80.5%, respectively. Freedom from recurrent IE was 96.4% at 20 years. Number of previous operations (hazard ratio (HR): 1.585, p=0.005), gram-negative bacteria (HR: 11.475, p<0.001), emergency operations (HR: 17.988, p=0.001), and longer aortic cross-clamp time (HR: 1.011, p=0.043) were risk factors for mortality.
In children and adults with CHD, mortality following surgery for IE was low, and recurrent IE was rare. Individualized management based on the patient's preoperative condition and the causative organism appears to be important for improving survival.

title: Multilayer regulation of osteogenic reprogramming in human aortic valve interstitial cells in calcific aortic valve disease.
authors: Chunyang Liang; Linwen Zhu; Min Zhou; Huoshun Shi; Guofeng Shao
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is an active fibrocalcific disorder in which human aortic valve interstitial cells (hVICs) undergo heterogeneous osteogenic reprogramming. This narrative review provides an hVIC-centered synthesis of four interacting regulatory layers: pathological microenvironmental cues, intracellular signaling, non-coding RNA regulation, and cellular heterogeneity. Lipid dysregulation, inflammation, hypoxia, oxidative and metabolic stress, cellular senescence, and abnormal mechanical loading alter hVIC behavior through interconnected developmental, inflammatory, metabolic, and mechanosensitive pathways. Non-coding RNAs add post-transcriptional and epigenetic regulation, although many proposed axes remain incompletely validated. Single-cell transcriptomic studies further identify distinct disease-associated hVIC states and challenge a universal linear transition from quiescent to myofibroblast-like and osteogenic cells. We compare conventional and advanced experimental models and evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies according to the strength of human, functional, and translational evidence. Current data support a context- and stage-dependent network rather than a single dominant pathway. Integrating human valve tissue, cell-state-resolved analyses, complementary disease models, clinically meaningful endpoints, and targeted delivery may improve biomarker development and support disease-modifying strategies for CAVD.

title: Machine Learning-Based Clustering of Clinical Phenotypes in Adults With Bicuspid Aortic Valve: A Large Single-Center Study.
authors: Xinyue Zhang; Zhuo Chen; Zhaokai Xu; Tingting Liu; Lixin Zhang; Yihua He; Xiaoyan Gu
abstract:
Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is clinically heterogeneous, and the relationships among valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, and aortic involvement remain incompletely understood. We aimed to identify clinical phenotypes of adults with BAV by clustering multidimensional clinical data, primarily echocardiographic parameters.
We retrospectively included adults with echocardiographically confirmed BAV at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2016 and December 2024. Data from the first echocardiographic examination and contemporaneous clinical records were extracted, and nine continuous and three categorical variables were entered into a two-step clustering model. Continuous and categorical variables were compared across clusters using the Kruskal-Wallis H test and chi-square test, respectively, followed by pairwise comparisons. The stability of the four-cluster solution was assessed using 100 bootstrap resamples; agreement was quantified with the adjusted Rand index (ARI) and Jaccard coefficients. Clustering was also repeated after separately excluding sex and valve dysfunction to assess the influence of these key variables on cluster structure.
A total of 6977 patients with echocardiographically diagnosed BAV were included. The median age was 53.0 years (interquartile range, 40.0-61.0), and 70.0% were men. Two-step clustering identified four clinical phenotypes that differed significantly in valve morphology, valvular dysfunction, aortic dimensions, left-heart remodeling, cardiac function, and surgical interventions (all p < 0.001): Cluster 1, a predominantly male, regurgitation-predominant phenotype with left ventricular dilatation; Cluster 2, a predominantly male, stenosis-predominant phenotype with concentric hypertrophy; Cluster 3, a male phenotype with no or mild valve dysfunction; and Cluster 4, a female phenotype characterized mainly by no or mild valve dysfunction with a tendency toward stenosis. The proportion undergoing subsequent surgery after the baseline echocardiographic assessment was highest in Cluster 2 (40%) and lowest in Cluster 3 (14%). Left ventricular end-systolic diameter, left ventricular end-diastolic diameter, aortic root diameter, valve dysfunction, and sex were the principal drivers of clustering. Across bootstrap resamples, the mean ARI for the four-cluster solution was 0.696. In sensitivity analyses, exclusion of either sex or valve dysfunction reduced the optimal solution from four clusters to two.
Machine learning-based two-step clustering identified four baseline clinical phenotypes among adults with BAV, revealing multidimensional combinations of valve morphology, valvular function, aortic dimensions, and left-heart remodeling. This classification is intended primarily to characterize the clinical heterogeneity of adult BAV; its longitudinal clinical value requires confirmation in independent prospective cohorts.

title: Dynamic Transmitral Gradient From Eccentric Aortic Regurgitation Resolved by Valve-in-Valve TAVR.
authors: Ishita Ray; Sami Shoura; Ragavendar Saravanabavanandan; Kyle Coombes; Rajvardhan Sisodia; Michael Z Grzeskowiak; Sudhir Mungee; Marco A Barzallo
abstract:
Bioprosthetic aortic valve degeneration can present as isolated regurgitant failure, and an eccentric jet may raise the transmitral gradient, mimicking mitral stenosis.
An 84-year-old man presented with acute heart failure 12 years after surgical aortic valve replacement. Echocardiography showed a degenerated Trifecta bioprosthesis with an immobile leaflet causing severe eccentric aortic regurgitation, whose jet impinged on the anterior mitral leaflet and produced severe functional mitral stenosis. Given high surgical risk, the heart team performed transfemoral valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
Trifecta leaflet tear causes regurgitant rather than stenotic failure; an eccentric jet can raise the transmitral gradient independent of the Austin Flint murmur. Valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement eliminated the regurgitation, improved leaflet mobility, and reduced the mean mitral gradient from 17 to 6 mm Hg, with complete symptom resolution.
Eccentric aortic regurgitation can cause a reversible rise in transmitral gradient; treating it can resolve apparent mitral stenosis without mitral intervention.

title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
authors: Kajetan Grodecki; Nipun Manral; Jacek Kwiecinski; Joel Lenell; Sebastien Cadet; Tara Zuhair Kassem; Jolien Geers; Caroline Park; Emily Xing; Guadalupe Flores Tomasino; Anna Olasinska-Wisniewska; Rafal Wolny; Maciej Dabrowski; Marcin Protasiewicz; Zbigniew Chmielak; Wojciech Wojakowski; Julia Niemierko; Jadwiga Fijalkowska; Bartosz Rymuza; Radoslaw Parma; Piotr Scislo; Marcin Grabowski; Dariusz Jagielak; Andrzej Walczak; Adrianna Hajder; Matylda Grodecka; Radoslaw Gocol; Tomasz Urbanowicz; Bartłomiej Perek; Marek Jemielity; Krzysztof Reczuch; Marek Grygier; Philipp Ruile; Simon Schoechlin; Hesham Elzomor; Michelle C Williams; Marc R Dweck; Daniel S Berman; David E Newby; Janusz Kochman; Hasan Jilaihawi; Raj Makkar; Piotr J Slomka; Adam Witkowski; Zenon Huczek; Damini Dey
abstract:
Computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables assessment of aortic valve tissue composition, providing insights into disease progression and helping predict outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis (AS). The authors aimed to develop a deep learning system for CTA-based quantification of aortic fibrotic and calcific tissue, validate its agreement with expert manual analysis and histopathology, and evaluate its value for outcome prediction.
This international, multicenter study included 1,674 patients who underwent CTA at 9 sites. A deep learning model based on the nnU-Net architecture was trained in 468 patients and applied to an external test set of 1,206 patients, including 29 with valve histology and 12 with serial CTA. In 1,165 patients with clinical outcomes, prognostic value was assessed adjusting for clinical, echocardiographic, and procedural covariates.
Deep learning-enabled tissue composition analysis was rapid (1.35 ± 0.4 min vs 7.2 ± 1.2 min for experts) with excellent agreement vs expert assessment (r = 0.915; intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.913), histology (r = 0.909; ICC = 0.905), and scan-rescan reproducibility (r = 0.999; ICC = 0.999). In the external cohort, 469 patients (40%) died over 4.1 ± 1.1 years of follow-up. Fibrotic tissue volume (adjusted HR [aHR] 1.42 per IQR increase; P < 0.001), calcific tissue attenuation (aHR 1.02 per 25 HU increase; P = 0.005), left ventricular ejection fraction (aHR 1.10 per 5% decrease; P < 0.001), life-threatening bleeding (aHR: 1.96; P = 0.003), major vascular complication (aHR: 1.51; P = 0.042) and postprocedural peak pressure gradient (aHR 1.03 per 1 mm Hg increase; P < 0.001) independently predicted mortality. Patients in the highest tertile of fibrotic tissue volume (>0.940 cm3) had a 2-fold higher risk of death (aHR: 2.0; P < 0.001), whereas patients with dense calcific tissue attenuation (>885 HU) had a 1.5-fold higher risk of death.
Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

title: From Anatomy to Tissue: Cardiac CT Finally Turns Its Attention to the Aortic Valve.
authors: Saima Mushtaq; Gianluca Pontone

title: Percutaneous Rescue of Acute Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction After Mitral Valve-In-Valve Replacement.
authors: Andrea Mangiameli; Valentina Bernardini; Alessia Azzano; Eligio Miccichè; Elvis Brscic; Andrea Cascella; Rocco Mollace; Davide Cao
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Mitral valve-in-valve procedures are generally associated with a lower risk of LVOTO because of the predictable geometry provided by the surgical bioprosthesis, yet severe obstruction may still occur and precipitate abrupt hemodynamic collapse.
A 79-year-old woman with a degenerated 27-mm Carpentier-Edwards Perimount mitral bioprosthesis presented with acute decompensated heart failure due to severe bioprosthetic mitral stenosis. Following multidisciplinary Heart Team evaluation, she was considered not a candidate for redo mitral valve surgery and underwent urgent transseptal valve-in-valve TMVR with a 26-mm balloon-expandable SAPIEN valve.
Immediately after valve deployment, severe LVOTO developed, with an invasive peak-to-peak LV-aortic gradient of 120 mmHg. A mechanism-guided percutaneous rescue strategy was undertaken. Correction of the structural component of obstruction reduced the gradient to 60 mmHg. Persistent obstruction suggested a significant dynamic contribution, prompting selective septal branch coil embolization, which further reduced the gradient to 20 mmHg and resulted in immediate hemodynamic stabilization.
Severe LVOTO after valve-in-valve TMVR may reflect both structural and dynamic mechanisms. Persistence of significant obstruction after structural correction should prompt consideration of a dynamic component and may guide effective rescue therapy.

title: Aortic annular enlargement using the Yang technique: the first reported case in the Peruvian Ministry of Health.
authors: Marycielo A Valdez; Edmy Callalli Matos; Silvana Gonzales
journal: Archivos peruanos de cardiologia y cirugia cardiovascular
abstract: Prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) remains an important limitation in patients with a small aortic annulus undergoing surgical aortic valve replacement. The Yang technique (Y-incision) has recently emerged as an effective alternative for achieving greater aortic annular enlargement while maintaining favorable perioperative outcomes. We report the first case of aortic annular enlargement using the Yang technique performed at our institution in a 56-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis and a small aortic annulus. Intraoperative evaluation revealed a 19-mm aortic annulus. After enlargement via a Y-incision and reconstruction with a bovine pericardial patch, a 23-mm mechanical prosthesis was successfully implanted without perioperative complications. Postoperative echocardiography demonstrated adequate prosthetic function, with a significant reduction in transvalvular gradients. Our initial experience suggests that the Yang technique is a safe, reproducible, and feasible option for centers introducing this procedure into their surgical practice. Although limited to a single case, the favorable outcome has encouraged our team to continue performing this technique in carefully selected patients.

title: Anesthetic Management of Pregnant Patients With Cardiovascular Disease: A Practical, Lesion-Based Clinical Review.
authors: Alexander Iosovich; Alexander Ronenson; Emilia Guasch; Nicolas Brogly; Yahya Aljuba; Daniel Shatalin
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality and increasingly complicates pregnancy as more women with congenital and acquired heart disease reach reproductive age. Anesthetic management of these patients requires integrating lesion-specific cardiovascular physiology, pregnancy-related hemodynamic changes, obstetric considerations, and the anticipated effects of labor, anesthesia, delivery, hemorrhage, and the postpartum transition. Despite contemporary cardiovascular and obstetric guidelines, translating lesion-specific physiology into practical anesthetic decisions remains challenging. This narrative review provides a practical framework for the peripartum anesthetic management of pregnant patients with CVD. We discuss contemporary risk assessment using the modified World Health Organization 2.0 classification and the Cardiac Disease in Pregnancy II risk model, followed by principles of Pregnancy Heart Team planning, labor analgesia, cesarean delivery, monitoring, anticoagulation, uterotonic therapy, and postpartum surveillance. Lesion-specific considerations are reviewed for mitral stenosis, aortic stenosis, aortic disease and coarctation, pulmonary hypertension, pregnancy-associated myocardial infarction, peripartum cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, and Fontan circulation. Particular attention is given to maintaining appropriate preload, ventricular filling, systemic vascular resistance, cardiac rhythm, and oxygenation while avoiding abrupt changes in vascular resistance or cardiac loading conditions. The review emphasizes individualized anesthetic planning rather than universal preferences for a particular anesthetic technique or mode of delivery. Neuraxial anesthesia can be advantageous in selected patients but should be considered in the context of ventricular function, pulmonary pressures, anticoagulation, urgency, and the expected hemodynamic response. General anesthesia remains an important option when neuraxial anesthesia is contraindicated or inadequate, rapid delivery is required, airway or ventilatory control is necessary, or maternal or surgical circumstances dictate. Uterotonic therapy should similarly be individualized according to cardiovascular physiology, with careful attention to dose, route, and hemodynamic effects. Close multidisciplinary planning and coordinated postpartum care are particularly important for women with pulmonary hypertension, ventricular dysfunction, complex congenital heart disease, and Fontan circulation.

title: Left Atrial Functional Parameters and Left Ventricular Reverse Remodeling After Aortic Valve Replacement in Severe Aortic Stenosis.
authors: Na Chen; Yongxin Li; Siqi Cao; Wenhui Gu; Huiyu Tang; Siyao Sun; Tao Cong; Haibo Wu; Jun Wu
abstract:
Left ventricular reverse remodeling (LVRR) after aortic valve replacement (AVR) varies in severe aortic stenosis (AS). We evaluated whether preoperative left atrial (LA)-derived functional indices were associated with structural LVRR (S-LVRR) and functional LVRR (F-LVRR).
This retrospective 2-center study included 139 adults with severe AS undergoing surgical or transcatheter AVR and follow-up echocardiography after a median of 6.1 months. S-LVRR was defined as normalization of left ventricular (LV) mass index, and F-LVRR as sex-specific recovery of absolute LV global longitudinal strain. Separate adjusted logistic models assessed LA reservoir strain (LASr), LA stiffness index (LASI), LA reservoir work, and LA volumetric/mechanical coupling index, with supportive sensitivity analyses.
S-LVRR and F-LVRR occurred in 58 (41.7%) and 42 (30.2%) patients, respectively. Higher LASr and lower LASI were independently associated with S-LVRR (odds ratio [OR] per 1-standard deviation increase, 2.48; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.37-4.49 and OR, 0.32; 95% CI, 0.13-0.79) and F-LVRR (OR, 7.41; 95% CI, 2.70-20.32 and OR, 0.01; 95% CI, 0.00-0.15). LASr remained robust across sensitivity analyses, whereas LASI was attenuated in change-based analyses.
In severe AS, preserved preoperative LASr and lower LASI were associated with postoperative LVRR after AVR. LASr was the most consistent LA-derived marker and may complement conventional LV assessment pending prospective validation.

title: The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
authors: Cristiano Spadaccio; Stefano Schena; Andrew J Sherman
journal: Europace : European pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac electrophysiology : journal of the working groups on cardiac pacing, arrhythmias, and cardiac cellular electrophysiology of the European Society of Cardiology
abstract: The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this direction-aortic valve stenosis is now managed through a multidisciplinary team that integrates anatomy, timing, procedural durability, and long-term risk across the full patient trajectory. We propose an AF Heart Team framework for non-paroxysmal AF in which catheter-based, hybrid, and surgical strategies are selected according to disease phenotype and lifetime trajectory, with the goal of intervening before advanced remodeling reduces the likelihood of durable rhythm control.

title: Variations in Access to Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement by Socioeconomic Factors: A Retrospective Population-Level Study in New South Wales, Australia.
authors: Md Shajedur Rahman Shawon; Jonathon B Ryan; Louisa Jorm
abstract:
Despite increasing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) activity in Australia in recent years, patient access to TAVI remains limited and is often more complex than access to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). The aim of this study was to identify socioeconomic factors associated with the likelihood of receiving TAVI versus SAVR in New South Wales (NSW), Australia.
Data from the NSW Admitted Patient Data Collection were used to compare the clinical and socioeconomic profiles of patients aged ≥65 years who underwent either TAVI or SAVR between 1 November 2017 and 28 February 2022. Multiple logistic regression analyses were performed on the overall patient cohort and on subgroups defined by age groups, hospital type and funding type.
The study included 6,493 patients (mean age: 79.1 years, 35.5% female) who underwent aortic valve replacement (SAVR=3,294; TAVI=3,199). The odds of receiving TAVI versus SAVR increased significantly with age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] for patients aged 85 years and older versus those aged 75-84 years: 12.3, 95% CI: 9.99-15.2). Patients from the most disadvantaged socioeconomic areas had lower odds of receiving TAVI than those from the least disadvantaged areas (aOR:0.58, 95% CI: 0.47-0.73). Patients with private health insurance/Department of Veterans Affairs (PHI/DVA) funding were more likely to receive TAVI than SAVR (aOR: 3.29, 95% CI: 2.61-4.14), with this finding consistent across age groups and even more pronounced in patients treated in public hospitals (aOR: 5.82, 95% CI: 4.40-7.70).
Our study highlights significant variations in TAVI access based on age, socioeconomic status of area of residence, and funding type. These findings underscore the need for policy settings that promote equitable access and ensure that procedural choices for aortic valve replacement reflect clinical needs.

title: [Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Coronary Arteritis Induced by Myeloproliferative Neoplasms:Report of a Case].
authors: Zaiqiang Yu; Shuto Watanabe; Kenyu Murata; Yuki Imamura; Masahito Minakawa
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
abstract: In a 60-year-old man with a history of stroke, coronary angiography revealed triple vessel disease, comprising left anterior descending artery (LAD) #6-7 with 99% diffuse stenosis within the stent, #11 and #12 with 90% stenosis, and right coronary artery (RCA) #1 stent with 50% stenosis. Cardiac ultrasonography showed 34% left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) without mitral regurgitation (MR) or tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Following median sternotomy, the bilateral internal thoracic artery (BITA) was harvested by skeletonization;however, dissection was confirmed at the distal end of the right internal thoracic artery (RITA). Owing to severe apical adhesions, we decided to perform on-pump beating coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) for this patient. Cardiopulmonary bypass was initiated via proximal aortic arch inflow and bicaval drainage without left ventricule (LV) venting. Subsequently, a left internal thoracic surgery (LITA)-free RITA composite Y-graft was prepared. On-pump beating CABG was performed in the graft design of the LITA-LAD (onlay patch, 4.5 cm), LITA-free RITA composite Y-graft to the obtuse marginal (OM) artery, and AO-saphenous vein graft (SVG)-4 posterior descending artery (PD)-4AV by sequential anastomosis. Many inflammatory cells invaded the RITA and coronary artery, and distal vessel thickening was confirmed but not in the ascending aorta. Coronary arteritis induced by myeloproliferative neoplasms was diagnosed based on pathology. Coronary computed tomography (CT) revealed the patency of all grafts.

title: [Non-anatomic Bypass for Severe Brachiocephalic Artery Stenosis due to Dissecting Aneurysm After Total Arch Aortic Replacement for Stanford Type A Acute Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
authors: Hana Fukuta; Ryohei Ushioda; Masahiko Narita; Yuki Setogawa; Hiroyuki Miyamoto; Ryo Okubo; Shogo Takahashi; Daisuke Takeyoshi; Shingo Kunioka; Masahiro Tsutsui; Hiroyuki Kamiya
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
abstract: Dissecting brachiocephalic artery aneurysm after total arch aortic replacement poses a risk of postoperative cerebral infarction, yet no consensus exists regarding optimal management. Treatment decisions rely on the patient's condition, degree of true lumen stenosis, and lesion characteristics. We report a case of a dissecting brachiocephalic aneurysm with severe true lumen stenosis following surgery for Stanford type A acute aortic dissection. A 70-year-old man was transferred to our hospital with acute aortic dissection and multiple right-hemispheric cerebral infarctions and underwent emergency total arch replacement. On postoperative day nine, contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed progressive false lumen expansion with significant true lumen compression. To prevent further cerebral ischemia, a left axillary-right common carotid artery non-anatomic bypass was performed. The patient gradually recovered left upper limb function and was transferred for rehabilitation on postoperative day 27.

title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Trace Visualization of the Central Retinal Artery: A Favorable Sign for Late-Window Endovascular Therapy in Central Retinal Artery Occlusion.
authors: Yang Du; Zhongqi Qi; Lu Cong; Dong Wang; Wanhu Liu; Shuo Zhang
abstract: In acute central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO), vessel stenosis and hemodynamic impairment significantly affect visual prognosis. We report a 69-year-old man who presented with 18 hours of acute, severe right eye blurred vision. Fundus examination and optical coherence tomography confirmed central retinal artery (CRA) occlusion with inner retinal edema. Digital subtraction angiography revealed an aortic arch variation and severe C1 segment stenosis of the right internal carotid artery (ICA), accompanied by delayed ophthalmic artery filling and faint visualization of the CRA. After multidisciplinary consultation, the patient underwent ICA stenting. Postoperative imaging showed resolved stenosis and improved retinal perfusion; the patient's vision subsequently improved and stabilized. This case suggests that revascularization can facilitate visual recovery even beyond the traditional window. Furthermore, faint CRA visualization on digital subtraction angiography indicates residual flow, providing a potential rationale for recanalization therapy.

journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Practical Solutions to Common TAVI Complications
authors: Herbert Kroon
abstract: Aortic valve stenosis Calcific aortic valve degeneration mainly affects the elderly population. Approximately 15% of elderly patients have some degree of aortic stenosis (AS)1. Untreated severe AS will lead to heart failure, angina and/or syncope and approximately half of patients will expire within 2 years after symptom onset1, 2. Historically, open heart surgery was the only treatment for severe AS. However, advanced age was a dominant argument to defer surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) was contrived as a less invasive alternative to surgery and to fulfill this unmet clinical need. After the first-in-human procedure in 2002, TAVI matured into a guideline recommended treatment of symptomatic severe AS in elderly patients across the entire risk spectrum3-7. Peri-procedural embolization Operator experience, improved planning and implantation strategies and multiple device iterations including smaller profile, repositioning ability and outer sealing fabric converted TAVI into a reproducible and relatively safe procedure8. However, the “Big Five” of complications in the modern TAVI era remain 1) access site complications and bleedings, 2) paravalvular leakage (PVL), 3) acute kidney injury (AKI), 4) conduction disturbances including the need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) and 5) stroke9. Up to 5% of patients suffer a neurological event after TAVI, mainly within the first 48 hours8, 10, 11. This finding suggests a direct causative role with the transcatheter valve implantation itself. Transcranial Doppler and brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) studies revealed debris embolization towards the brain and new brain lesions after TAVI in the vast majority of patients12-15. Most of these embolizations remain clinically silent at first sight but may be linked to neurocognitive decline and frank dementia16. Embolic protection devices (EPD) have been developed to deflect or capture embolized debris on its way to the brain and may possibly reduce brain lesions and neurological events including stroke and neurocognitive decline. Part I of this thesis adds perspective to the etiopathology of TAVI related stroke and the mechanism of action of the current spectrum of cerebral embolic protection devices. We also present insights into the microscopic analysis of debris that was captured with filters during TAVI procedures. Vascular access and complications 1 TAVI typically requires large bore femoral artery access. By default, larger arteriotomies are at higher risk for access site complications and bleedings. A completely percutaneous approach relies on vascular access closure devices (VCD) to manage the arteriotomy and provide patent hemostasis. TAVI in low to intermediate risk patients is associated with a major vascular complication rate ranging between 2 and 8%4, 11. The conventional closure technique is based on sutures and most access site complications after TAVI procedures are related to closure device failure17. A collagen plug based closure device was introduced as an alternative to sutures. Part II of this thesis addresses vascular complications and provides information on clinical outcomes with collagen plug-based VCD. TAVI-related conduction disturbances Acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI are frequent and may lead to heart failure (re-) admissions and impaired long-term prognosis18-22. The atrioventricular bundle pierces the membranous septum between the right and non-coronary cusp of the aortic valve and surfaces along the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT), which makes it vulnerable to contact pressure by the implanted transcatheter heart valve (THV) during TAVI23, 24. New left bundle branch block (LBBB) and third-degree atrioventricular block (AV3B) requiring PPI occur in up to a third and quarter of patients, respectively18-22. These conduction disturbances may be transient or remain permanent which is clinically relevant in view of in-hospital stay and overall healthcare costs. Unfortunately, there are no uniform definitions to describe conduction dynamics post-TAVI. Inconsistent reporting makes the interpretation of the literature on this topic challenging. Part III of this thesis will elaborate on what is currently known about the incidence of newly acquired conduction disturbances after TAVI and studies specific features on the baseline and postprocedural electrocardiogram (ECG) to predict conduction dynamics. These insights may help determine the need and timing of PPI and adjust hospital discharge policies.

title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance feature-tracking strain characterization across phenotypic spectrum of danon disease
authors: Guijuan Cao; Ni Liu; Jinghui Li; Zixian Chen; Gang Yin; Weipeng Yan; Xiang Wang; Chen Cui; Minjie Lu
journal: The International Journal of Cardiovascular Imaging
abstract: To characterize atrial and ventricular strain across the phenotypic spectrum of Danon disease (DD) and explore their relationships with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent. This retrospective case-control study included 27 DD patients (median age 17 [range 10–50] years; 15 males) and 32 healthy controls. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging was performed at 3-T with cine and LGE. Structural, functional, and LGE parameters were assessed. Kruskal-Wallis H test with Dunn’s test and Bonferroni correction was used for intergroup comparisons; Mann-Whitney U or t-test for two-group comparisons; Spearman’s correlation; and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were used. Left atrial (LA) and right atrial (RA) strain were impaired across all DD subgroups versus controls, with LA strain impairment evident even in the hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) subgroup with preserved LVEF. LV global longitudinal strain (LV-GLS) was reduced across all subgroups, whereas global circumferential strain (GCS) and global radial strain (GRS) impairment were confined to hypertrophic and dilated cardiomyopathy (HCM-DCM) and dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) subgroups. Mid-ventricular longitudinal strain was relatively preserved ( P = 0.062). LGE extent correlated with GRS (all P < 0.01). Left atrial conduit strain rate (LASRe) demonstrated the best diagnostic performance (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.981; sensitivity 88.9%, specificity 100%). CMR feature-tracking revealed phenotype-specific bi-atrial and biventricular strain abnormalities in DD. Atrial strain impairment was detectable even in HCM with preserved LVEF, suggesting early mechanical dysfunction. LASRe showed promising discrimination and warrants validation. HCM-DCM may represent a possible transitional phenotype; longitudinal validation is required.

journal: European Heart Journal - Valvular and Structural Heart Disease
abstract: Abstract Background Functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) is a highly dynamic disease. Some patients exhibit only moderate (2+) FMR at rest, which deteriorates to moderate-to-severe or severe FMR (3+ or 4+) during stress, with effective regurgitant orifice area (EROA) increased ≥0.1 cm2—termed dynamic severe FMR. Observational studies link this condition to worse outcomes, with mitral valve intervention offering potential benefits; however, high-quality evidence remains deficient. Aims The Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair In dynaMic sEvere functional mitral Regurgitation (TIMER) trial aims to assess the safety and effectiveness of transcatheter edge-to-edge repair plus guideline-directed medical therapy versus guideline-directed medical therapy alone in symptomatic chronic heart failure patients with dynamic severe FMR, defined as moderate (2+) regurgitation at rest (EROA ≥0.2 cm2 to <0.3 cm2 and/or regurgitant volume (RVol) ≥30 mL/beat to <45 mL/beat), deteriorating to moderate-to-severe or severe (3+ or 4+) during handgrip stress echocardiography (stress EROA ≥0.30 cm2 and/or RVol ≥45 mL/beat), with EROA increased ≥0.1 cm2. Methods This prospective, multicentre, randomised trial enrols patients with dynamic severe FMR confirmed by a core laboratory using handgrip stress echocardiography, across 20 participating centres in China. Patients are randomised 1:1 to transcatheter edge-to-edge repair plus medical therapy or medical therapy alone. The primary endpoint is the composite incidence of cardiovascular death and all heart failure hospitalisations during the entire follow-up period. Conclusion This trial will provide critical evidence on transcatheter edge-to-edge repair in patients with dynamic severe FMR, informing future treatment recommendations. Trial registration number: NCT07197021

title: Association of pre-transplant right ventricular function parameters with long-term cardiovascular outcomes following kidney transplantation
authors: Cayden Lawrence; Rushda Faruk Mansuri; Reem S. Ahmed; Ava DeLonais-Parker; Zalan Shah; Yang Lyu; Ananta Sriram; James Roe; Elsa Treiber; Katherine Desanti; Krista L. Lentine; Mina Mecheal Benjamin
journal: The International Journal of Cardiovascular Imaging
abstract: Abstract The hemodynamic effects of end-stage kidney disease and associated pulmonary hypertension may impair right ventricular (RV) function and influence cardiovascular (CV) outcomes after kidney transplantation (KT). We aimed to evaluate the association between pre-transplant echocardiographic RV function parameters, including RV strain, and long-term CV outcomes following KT. In this retrospective cohort study, we included adult KT recipients at a single Midwest academic center from 2015 to 2024 who had adequate-quality pre-transplant echocardiograms and follow-up at our institution. RV function parameters included tricuspid annular systolic velocity (S′), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), fractional area change (FAC), RV index of myocardial performance (RIMP), and RV free wall strain measured by two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of CV death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular accident, heart failure hospitalization, coronary revascularization, or sustained ventricular arrhythmias. Among 371 patients (mean age 53.5 ± 13.1 years; 56% male) followed for a median of 4.9 years (IQR, 3.1–6.4), 79 (21.2%) experienced MACE. On univariable Cox analysis, RIMP and RV strain parameters were associated with MACE, whereas S′, TAPSE, and FAC were not. Kaplan–Meier analysis showed lower MACE-free survival in patients with abnormal mid and apical RV strain, whereas the basal and dichotomized average-strain comparisons were not significant. In multivariable models, only average, mid, and apical RV strain remained independently associated with MACE. Pre-transplant RV strain was independently associated with long-term MACE after KT and may aid CV risk stratification. Further studies are needed to validate these findings.
