title: Contemporary Updates in Lung Transplantation: a Perioperative and Critical Care Anesthesiology Perspective
authors: Jennifer Boleyn; Christina Anne Jelly; Frederick W. Lombard; Anna Eid; John Bryant
abstract: Abstract Purpose of Review This review reports advances from the past five years in the perioperative and critical care management of lung transplantation, emphasizing donor pool expansion, selection of intraoperative mechanical support, ventilation of the allograft, and mitigation of primary graft dysfunction. Recent Findings Ex vivo lung perfusion and donation after circulatory death, with normothermic regional perfusion, have enlarged the usable donor pool. Observational data and 2026 consensus statements favor venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation over cardiopulmonary bypass when intraoperative support is required, although those data cannot evaluate a planned routine support strategy. Ventilation of the allograft is becoming graft-specific rather than borrowed from acute respiratory distress syndrome practice, and enhanced recovery pathways with regional analgesia are being applied across the perioperative continuum. Summary Perioperative anesthesia management materially influences lung transplant outcomes. Priorities for future work include standardized intraoperative extracorporeal membrane oxygenation protocols, individualized ventilation, opioid-sparing analgesia, and prevention of chronic lung allograft dysfunction.

title: CT and MRI in periprocedural transcatheter mitral valve replacement: expert recommendations by the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI)
authors: Anna Palmisano; Marco Francone; Prabhakar Shantha Rajiah; Jonathon Leipsic; Gudrun Maria Feuchtner; Matthias Eberhard; Ricardo P.J. Budde; Bradley D. Allen; Hatem Alkadhi; Antonio Esposito
abstract: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is a minimally invasive treatment option for symptomatic patients with severe mitral valve disease who are at high surgical risk or ineligible for open-heart surgery. The procedure has been associated with improved quality of life and functional status in selected patients and is increasingly recognized as a valuable therapeutic option in the management of complex mitral valve disorders. A multidisciplinary Heart Team is essential to ensure the clinical success of TMVR, and imaging specialists play a central role in the preprocedural assessment for patient and device selection, during the procedure, to guide and monitor the implantation, and after the procedure, for follow-up and for the correct diagnosis of short- or long-term complications. Echocardiography is required for initial diagnosis, for assessment of valve hemodynamics, intraprocedural guidance and monitoring. However, a multimodality approach including CT and/or MRI is frequently needed to correctly manage the phase of preprocedural planning and the diagnosis of complications. This consensus document, developed by a working group of experts from the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI), provides evidence-based recommendations for CT and cardiac MRI acquisition and post-processing in procedural planning and postprocedural evaluation in patients undergoing TMVR. Emphasis is placed on the technical requirements and standardization of imaging protocols, which must account for the heterogeneity of imaging equipment used in clinical settings. The document also outlines recommendations for all necessary preprocedural measures to ensure consistency, accuracy, and effective communication among specialists. KEY POINTS: Question How can CT and MRI acquisition, measurement, and reporting for TMVR be standardized to support accurate procedural planning, device selection, and follow-up? Findings This expert consensus provides recommendations for standardized CT and MRI protocols, key measurements, and structured reporting throughout TMVR planning and follow-up. Clinical relevance CT and MRI assessment may improve patient selection, procedural planning, multidisciplinary communication, and detection of postprocedural complications, supporting safer and more consistent TMVR practice across centers.

title: Reduced apelin expression and atrial fibrosis in postoperative atrial fibrillation following coronary artery bypass grafting
authors: Yijun Xu; Zhi Chen; Peng Liu; Wen Wen; Xiaowei Li; Hao Wang
abstract: The role of apelin in atrial fibrosis linked to postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is not fully understood. This exploratory study investigated apelin's association with POAF-related atrial fibrosis and its impact on profibrotic signaling. The study included 18 patients: six CABG patients with POAF, six CABG patients without POAF, and six patients with congenital heart disease in sinus rhythm (serving as a secondary reference). Left atrial appendage tissue was analyzed histologically and molecularly, and serum apelin levels were measured on postoperative day 2 in CABG patients. Primary neonatal rat atrial fibroblasts were treated with transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) both with and without apelin, or subjected to apelin silencing. Compared with CABG patients without POAF, the POAF group exhibited lower atrial apelin expression and serum concentrations, increased collagen deposition, elevated TGF-β1 expression, and enhanced phosphorylation of mothers against decapentaplegic homolog 2 (Smad2), while total Smad2 remained unchanged. Experimentally, apelin attenuated TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation, collagen expression, and Smad2 phosphorylation. Conversely, apelin silencing increased the expression of fibrosis-associated proteins. These preliminary findings suggest a link between reduced apelin and atrial fibrosis, as well as POAF after CABG. They also indicate antifibrotic effects of apelin, potentially mediated through TGF-β1/Smad2 signaling. Further research with larger clinical cohorts and complementary experimental models is necessary to fully elucidate the pathway mediation and clinical significance of these findings.

title: Sequential Coronary Obstruction After Native TAVI: Immediate Acute Occlusion and Very Late Stent Compression by Aortic Wall Hematoma
authors: Ali Rıza Akyüz; Murat Gökhan Yerlikaya; Mustafa Öztürk; Selim Kul
abstract: Coronary obstruction is a rare but catastrophic complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) associated with high mortality. While acute and delayed presentations have distinct pathophysiological mechanisms, their occurrence in the same patient is exceedingly rare. We present a unique case of a 91-year-old female who developed acute left main coronary artery (LMCA) obstruction immediately following native TAVI using a balloon-expandable valve, which was successfully treated with bail-out percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Three months later (> 60 days, classified as "Very Late" coronary obstruction), she presented with severe angina and heart failure. Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) revealed extrinsic compression of the previously implanted coronary stent caused by a localized aortic wall hematoma. A repeat PCI with a stent-in-stent technique restored coronary flow, leading to complete clinical recovery. This case expands the known mechanical spectrum of very late coronary obstruction according to recent classification frameworks and highlights the vital role of intravascular imaging and multimodality assessment in diagnosis and management.

title: Role of protein lactylation in pulmonary and cardiovascular diseases: Current research and future perspectives (Review)
authors: Zi-an Pan; Li-ting Tong; Zhe-Min Wang
abstract: The cardiopulmonary system is highly coupled in structure and function. Metabolic and epigenetic disturbances constitute the common pathological basis for the progression of cardiopulmonary diseases and their comorbidities. Aberrant metabolic reprogramming triggers lactate accumulation. As a novel post-translational modification, protein lactylation participates in the regulation of inflammatory responses, cell death and fibrotic remodeling, thereby mediating cardiopulmonary dysfunction. Existing studies have separately illustrated the roles of lactylation in isolated pulmonary and cardiac disorders. Nevertheless, most investigations are confined to a single-organ perspective, lacking systematic summaries of common mechanisms for cardiopulmonary crosstalk and comorbidities. The present review summarized research advances of lactylation in various cardiopulmonary diseases, generalized its potential comorbid mechanisms, identified existing research gaps and translational obstacles for targeted therapy and collected lactylation-targeted intervention compounds with potential therapeutic effects reported in basic studies. The present review further outlined prospective research directions focused on spatiotemporal regulation of lactylation, metabolic-immune-epigenetic crosstalk that shapes disease progression, and the identification of specific targets in cardiopulmonary comorbidities, with the aim of providing a theoretical foundation for developing precise, broad-spectrum, co-targeted therapeutic strategies for cardiopulmonary diseases.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis in solid tumors: mutant hematopoietic cells as a tumor-microenvironment component across source, lineage and treatment
authors: Hang Su; Junli Tang; Linwei Li
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) introduces a hematopoietic component into the molecular and immune landscape of solid tumors. Its interpretation depends on whether a variant is measured in blood, plasma or tumor tissue, which cells carry it, and when sampling occurs relative to treatment. Existing reviews have examined cancer-associated inflammation, therapy-related clonal selection and clinical outcomes; a less developed question is how these observations can be compared when they measure different aspects of the same clone. This focused narrative review connects source attribution with immune-cell state, tissue localization and longitudinal change, separating human associations from cellular localization and experimental perturbation. Paired leukocyte analysis can identify hematopoietic variants that would otherwise be assigned to cancer cells. Mutation-resolved tissue measurements add information about local immune interactions, whereas serial blood measurements help distinguish clonal selection from the relative prominence of CH when tumor-derived plasma DNA declines. Genotype-specific findings, particularly involving TET2 and myeloid function, provide mechanistic explanations for some treatment associations, but aggregate CH has shown inconsistent relationships with immune-checkpoint efficacy and toxicity. The resulting framework links each measurement to its appropriate biological or clinical use: source correction is already actionable, while treatment prediction and organ-specific risk assessment require evidence that CH adds information beyond established tumor and patient characteristics.

title: Joint association and interaction of lipoprotein(a) and hyperuricemia with long-term outcomes in chronic total occlusion
authors: Jian Zhang; Bingbing Zhang; Jun Xie
abstract: Background Long-term outcomes differ substantially among patients with chronic total occlusion (CTO), and risk assessment remains challenging. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] and hyperuricemia are both associated with cardiovascular risk, but the prognostic significance of their coexistence in this population is uncertain. Methods We retrospectively studied 391 patients with angiographically confirmed CTO. Patients were classified into four groups according to baseline Lp(a) and uric acid (UA) levels: neither elevated, elevated lipoprotein(a) only, hyperuricemia only, and both elevated. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs), defined as the first occurrence of all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, target vessel revascularization, or stroke. Cox regression was used to assess long-term associations, while additive and multiplicative interactions were examined. Incremental prognostic value was evaluated using model discrimination, reclassification, calibration, and bootstrap internal validation. Results During a median follow-up of 73 months, event rates were 12.21%, 29.89%, 28.57%, and 66.27% across the four groups, respectively (P<0.001). Patients with both elevated lipoprotein(a) and hyperuricemia had the highest event risk compared with those with neither factor elevated (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 11.46, 95% confidence interval [CI] 6.44–20.41; P<0.001). In a sensitivity analysis restricted to all-cause death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or stroke, the association remained significant (aHR 4.23, 95% CI 2.13–8.39; P<0.001). A positive additive interaction was observed, whereas the multiplicative interaction was not significant. The apparent C-indices were 0.691 and 0.828 for the Base and Expanded models, respectively; after bootstrap optimism correction, the corresponding C-indices were 0.634 and 0.791. Conclusions Concurrent elevation of Lp(a) and UA was associated with higher long-term cardiovascular risk in patients with CTO and may provide prognostic information beyond either marker considered alone. These findings require external validation before the proposed dual-biomarker classification can be applied clinically.

title: Huaban Tongmai decoction attenuates ferroptosis-associated vascular inflammation in carotid artery atherosclerosis with involvement of the p53-Parkin mitophagy pathway
authors: Jiaxi Zou; Zhou Xiujuan; Ni Jin; Mei Lai; Liying He; Peiyang Gao
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract: Background Carotid artery atherosclerosis (CAS) is a chronic inflammatory vascular disease in which ferroptosis—an iron-dependent, oxidative form of regulated cell death—has been implicated in endothelial injury and vascular inflammatory responses. Despite growing evidence for the therapeutic potential of Huaban Tongmai decoction (HBTMD) against CAS, existing studies have not clearly elucidated its specific molecular mechanisms. This study focused on exploring and elucidating the mitigating mechanism of HBTMD against CAS. Methods An in vivo ApoE-/- mouse model of CAS was constructed via high-fat diet (HFD) combined with carotid ligation, and an ox-LDL-induced endothelial injury model using human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs). The chemical components of HBTMD were screened by UHPLC-MS/MS, and its marker constituents were quantified. Integrative proteomics and untargeted metabolomics identified key DEPs and metabolites related to HBTMD intervention. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations explored potential molecular interactions and candidate targets. Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1), Mdivi-1, and p53 siRNA were used in the indicated cell experiments to explore ferroptosis-associated injury and possible mitochondrial regulatory mechanisms. Results UHPLC-MS/MS identified 684 chemical constituents in HBTMD. Pharmacodynamic evaluation showed that HBTMD significantly reduced carotid lipid accumulation and plaque area in CAS mice. Integrated proteomic and metabolomic analyses suggested that modulation of autophagy and ferroptosis pathways may underlie HBTMD’s efficacy. Network pharmacology predicted p53 as a core target. Molecular docking and MD simulations suggested plausible interactions of spinosin and salvianolic acid A with p53, without establishing direct target engagement. In vitro and in vivo validation showed that HBTMD improved mitochondrial integrity, reduced inflammatory cytokines, and inhibited ferroptosis. HBTMD also lowered ROS and altered markers consistent with increased mitophagy-related activity; Mdivi-1 partially attenuated selected protective effects. The additional effects of HBTMD on several pathway-associated proteins were diminished after p53 knockdown, supporting the involvement of p53 but not establishing a complete causal pathway. Conclusion These preclinical findings suggest that HBTMD attenuates ferroptosis-associated endothelial injury and vascular inflammation in experimental CAS, accompanied by changes in p53-Parkin signaling and mitophagy-related markers. The pathway warrants further causal and translational validation.

title: Analysis of reproductive traits associated with lipoprotein(a) deficiency in participants from the Pakistan Genome Resource
authors: Christopher Koch; John E. Dominy; Allan M. Gurtan; Maleeha Zaman Khan; Shareef Khalid; Yoav Timsit; JP Casas; Carolina Hache; Huilei Xu; Michael Mendelson; Ieuan Jones; Allison B. Goldfine; Danish Saleheen
abstract: Aims. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined, independent risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, driving development of LPA-targeting therapies that markedly lower circulating Lp(a). Because LPA?the gene encoding apolipoprotein(a)?is absent in most model organisms, preclinical studies have limited value for assessing effects such as reproductive safety. Therefore, naturally occurring human LPA ?knockouts? were analyzed to evaluate reproductive outcomes of on-target Lp(a) lowering. Methods and Results. Individuals carrying high-confidence LPA loss-of-function (LoF) variants which reduce Lp(a) in a gene-dosage?dependent manner within the Pakistan Genome Resource were identified. LoF variants showed no depletion of homozygotes relative to Hardy?Weinberg expectations. LPA LoF associations with fertility-related traits (ever having a child and number of children) under additive and recessive models were assessed using regenie-based burden testing, including sex-stratified analyses, and no significant associations were observed. A recall-by-genotype study of female LoF homozygotes alongside heterozygous and non-carrier family member controls was performed, surveying reproductive histories and offspring outcomes. Across 107 pregnancies and 87 children in 19 homozygous LoF women, rates of miscarriage, maternal complications (including preeclampsia, hypertension, and gestational diabetes), delivery complications, neonatal intensive care admission, birth defects, and child health problems were comparable across genotypes with no statistically significant genotype?outcome associations. Conclusions. These genetic and by-genotype analyses indicate that complete lifelong LPA deficiency due to high-confidence LPA loss-of-function variants is not associated with overt adverse maternal fertility, pregnancy or child health outcomes. These findings offer human genetic reassurance regarding reproductive and developmental safety in the context of sustained Lp(a)-lowering, with implications for long-term therapies targeting Lp(a).

title: Estratificación del riesgo cardiovascular en el Perú: de los puntajes internacionales a la decisión clínica individualizada
authors: Jorge A. Pérez-Coaguila
abstract: ResumenLa estratificación del riesgo cardiovascular orienta las decisiones de prevención primaria, pero la utilidad de los puntajes depende de su desempeño en la población en la que se aplican.Esta revisión narrativa examina los principales modelos de predicción y su pertinencia para el Perú.Se discuten las limitaciones de extrapolar modelos internacionales y la necesidad de validación local.Asimismo, se revisa el papel de los modificadores clínicos y biológicos del riesgo, incluidos la lipoproteína(a), la inflamación, los antecedentes familiares y los factores reproductivos.Se analiza también la contribución de las técnicas de imagen para detectar aterosclerosis subclínica, así como el valor y las limitaciones del puntaje de calcio coronario.Se propone integrar la estimación del riesgo, los modificadores clínicos y la evaluación selectiva de la aterosclerosis subclínica para orientar decisiones preventivas individualizadas en el contexto peruano.

title: Angiopoetin-2 and IGFBP-7 as novel biomarkers of abnormal angiogenesis in von Willebrand disease
authors: Antoine Babuty; Valérie Horvais; Pierre Boisseau; Cloe Geay; Marc Trossaërt; Catherine Ternisien; Nicolas Drillaud; Yohann Repessé; Marc Fouassier
abstract: Abstract von Willebrand factor (VWF) is recognized as an active regulator of angiogenesis, particularly through control of the endothelial storage and release of angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2). This offers a plausible explanation for the poorly understood association between von Willebrand disease (VWD) and gastrointestinal (GI) angiodysplasia. However, the circulating angiogenic biomarker profile of patients with VWD remains partially characterized. This study was designed to comprehensively explore angiogenic mediators across VWD types/subtypes and determine their relationship with the VWF multimeric profile and GI bleeding/angiodysplasia phenotype. Seventy-six genetically confirmed patients with VWD and 30 healthy controls were included. A large panel of over 12 angiogenic mediators was assessed by multiplexed immunoassay. Peripheral levels of Ang-2, IGFBP-7 and angiostatin were significantly higher in type 2A and 2B VWD compared to controls and type 1 VWD. IGFBP-7 was significantly higher in patients with an abnormal multimeric profile. These markers did not correlate with VWF antigen or activity. Soluble TIE-2 was significantly lower and PDGF-AB significantly higher in patients with angiodysplasia. TRAIL and soluble VEGF-R2 were lower in patients with angiodysplasia or GI bleeding. No differences were observed for VEGF-A, VEGF-C/D, BMP-10 or endoglin. The structural integrity of VWF, rather than its plasma concentration, was associated with a distinct proangiogenic signature combining elevated Ang-2 and IGFBP-7 and reduced soluble TIE-2, supporting a role for VWF in the regulation of angiogenesis independent from its hemostatic function. Ang-2 and IGFBP-7 emerge as promising biomarkers and candidate therapeutic targets for VWD-associated angiodysplasia and GI bleeding, warranting validation in larger cohorts.

title: Galectin-9 drives thrombo-inflammatory circuits initiating venous thrombosis
authors: Akhil Antony Konkoth; Adel Abo Mansour; Katharine Whitworth; Ivan Budnik; Daniel Steiner; Cihan Ay; Danielle R. Lezama; Helen Michelle McGettrick; Dean Philip John Kavanagh; Francesco Μaione; Juma El-Awaisi; George Ed Rainger; Julie Rayes; Alexander G. Brill; Alexander G. Brill
abstract: Background: Venous thromboembolism is increasingly recognized as a thrombo-inflammatory disease, yet the pathways linking inflammation to venous thrombus initiation remain incompletely defined. Galectin-9 (Gal-9), a β-galactoside-binding lectin elevated in inflammatory disorders, has no defined role in venous thrombosis. Methods: Using plasma from patients with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), Gal-9-deficient mice, an inferior vena cava stenosis model, intravital microscopy, microfluidics, and ex vivo platelet and neutrophil assays, we assessed the functional contribution of Gal-9 to venous thrombosis. Results: Plasma Gal-9 was elevated in DVT patients, correlated with D-dimer at presentation, and declined over 3-month follow-up. Gal-9 deletion did not alter hemostasis but markedly impaired thrombus initiation, with reduced platelet and neutrophil recruitment to the vessel wall and reduced intra-thrombus neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. TNF-α/IFN-γ-stimulated endothelial cells upregulated Gal-9 and promoted platelet adhesion and fibrin(ogen) deposition, which Gal-9 neutralization partially reversed. Under venous shear, immobilized recombinant Gal-9 potentiated platelet activation and thrombus formation, particularly alongside collagen, whereas Gal-9 inhibition suppressed these responses. Gal-9-activated platelets promoted NETosis and shifted thrombus composition toward a NET-rich inflammatory phenotype. Conclusions: Gal-9 is a previously unrecognized driver of venous thrombo-inflammation, linking vascular inflammation to platelet activation, NET formation, and thrombosis. Genetic deletion attenuated these responses in vivo, and antibody-mediated Gal-9 neutralization suppressed platelet activation and thrombus formation in vitro, identifying the Gal-9 glycan-binding pathway as a therapeutic target that disrupts thrombosis without impairing hemostasis.

title: The “Peanut Sign” is a useful tool to detect spiral atrial septal defects
authors: Jule Marie Dittmer Hein; Anja Tengler; Nikolaus A. Haas
abstract: Spiral atrial septal defects may complicate transcatheter closure and increase the risk of device embolisation. We describe a 5-year-old boy with pulmonary stenosis and a secundum atrial septal defect in whom an initially implanted 9 mm device embolised. At repeat intervention, balloon sizing revealed a bilobed, peanut-shaped configuration with a double waist, suggestive of a spiral atrial septal defect. A 15 mm device was subsequently implanted, achieving stable closure. The "Peanut Sign" may serve as a useful marker for identifying spiral atrial septal defects and guiding appropriate device selection.

title: When the RotaWire Crosses but Cannot Advance: Dual‐Lumen Microcatheter–Assisted RotaWire Delivery
authors: Kazumasa Kurogi; Masanobu Ishii; Nobuyasu Yamamoto; Kenichi Tsujita
abstract: RotaWire delivery can be challenging in severely calcified device-uncrossable coronary lesions when conventional wire exchange through a microcatheter is not feasible. We report a 76-year-old man with a severely calcified mid-left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD) lesion in which neither a microcatheter nor a 0.75 mm balloon could cross. A second channel was created using a penetration wire through a dual-lumen microcatheter, allowing direct RotaWire crossing. However, the RotaWire could not be advanced sufficiently into the distal LAD. After intentional proximal pullback of the dual-lumen microcatheter, the microcatheter and RotaWire were held together and advanced as a single unit, enabling adequate distal RotaWire positioning and successful rotational atherectomy. This case highlights a distinct challenge after successful direct RotaWire crossing and demonstrates coupled advancement with a dual-lumen microcatheter as a potential bailout technique when distal RotaWire advancement remains difficult.

title: Descriptive analysis of mitral and tricuspid annular parameters in non-valvular atrial fibrillation
authors: 王吴刚; Xuejia Guo; Yanyan Zhang; Gaiqin Liu; Xinle Jia; Yandong Deng
abstract: The objective was to describe mitral and tricuspid annular parameters by regurgitation severity within non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), emphasizing estimation precision, with secondary clinical-comparator analyses. In this retrospective cross-sectional study, 190 records from a 2024–2025 echocardiography record set were assessed; 4 were excluded and 96 NVAF and 90 patent foramen ovale (PFO)-evaluation comparator records were included. Recorded maximal and minimal annular areas, recorded annular height (AHmax), and area change fraction (ACF) were analyzed. ACF required complete valid area pairs. Mean differences with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using Welch tests; matched comparisons used complete pairs and paired tests. Within NVAF, mean differences (moderate-or-greater minus less-than-moderate regurgitation; 95% CIs) were − 0.28 (− 0.64 to 0.08) mm for mitral AH max and − 0.31 (− 2.32 to 1.71) percentage points for mitral ACF. Corresponding tricuspid differences were − 0.28 (− 0.64 to 0.07) mm and − 1.08 (− 3.52 to 1.36) percentage points. Mitral areas were larger in the 14 patients with moderate-or-greater mitral regurgitation. Effective ACF sample sizes in NVAF were 92 and 91 for the mitral and tricuspid annuli. Quantitative grading was complete in 42 mitral and 34 tricuspid cases. Between-cohort contrasts were accompanied by substantial baseline imbalance and incomplete acquisition metadata. Within-NVAF recorded AHmax and ACF estimates were imprecise and did not establish equivalence. Tricuspid findings remain exploratory; recorded AHmax cannot establish three-dimensional non-planarity. Between-cohort contrasts cannot distinguish biological variation from differences in measurement or clinical context. Prospective studies with documented acquisition protocols, complete regurgitation grading, and longitudinal three-dimensional imaging are needed.

title: Mechanosensing channels PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 regulate mitral valve serotonin-mediated homeostasis and pathophysiology
authors: Stanley Stachelek; Robert LEVY; Emily Hall
abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) pathophysiology involves increased serotonin (5-HT) receptor (HTR) expression and signalling, together with reduced 5-HT transporter (SLC6A4) expression in mitral valve interstitial cells (MVIC). The mechanosensitive calcium channels, PIEZO1 and PIEZO2, regulate cellular responses to a variety of mechanical conditions; however, PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 have not been studied in MR. We investigated the hypothesis that PIEZO1 and PIEZO2 mediate, through 5-HT mechanisms, both homeostasis in normal mitral valves (nMV) and in the pathophysiology of MR.

title: Making Reynolds-number reasoning visible: complementary classroom models for plume organization and geometry–flow coupling
authors: Victor Akinyemi; Heidi L. Lujan; Stephen E. DiCarlo
abstract: Reynolds number is central to cardiovascular physiology, yet students often memorize the equation without understanding the competing inertial and viscous effects that it represents. We developed two complementary, low-cost classroom demonstrations intended to make selected relationships relevant to Reynolds-number reasoning visible without treating either apparatus as a quantitative Reynolds experiment. In the first, an adjustable aquarium air pump drives bubbles through submerged diffusers in transparent chambers. Changes in nominal pump drive and fluid composition produce qualitative changes in bubble rise, plume width, lateral motion, and plume organization. Because this is buoyant two-phase flow, these observations are not classifications of laminar or turbulent internal flow. In the second, aerosol generated by ultrasonic foggers is carried through nominal 5-mL and 50-mL serological pipettes and illuminated at the outlets. Changing pipette geometry changes flow resistance and can alter volumetric flow, internal and exit velocity, and jet momentum flux, but these quantities were not measured. The visible output is the external free jet; therefore, plume speed and coherence are described as apparent, qualitative observations rather than direct measures of internal velocity or Reynolds number. The activities use a predict-observe-explain sequence and connect cautiously to clinical examples as mechanistic analogies. This report describes qualitative instructional demonstrations, not a quantitative fluid-mechanics study or a formal educational-outcomes study.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Mitral Valve Surgery for Mitral Regurgitation in Patients With Marfan Syndrome ― A Retrospective Single-Center Study ―
authors: Yojiro Machii; Kota Suzuki; Naonori Kawamoto; Satoshi Kainuma; Kizuku Yamashita; Takashi Kakuta; Ayumi Ikuta; Rieko Kutsuzawa; Yuki Tadokoro; Satsuki Fukushima
abstract: Background: Because data on the long-term outcomes of surgical treatment for mitral valve (MV) disease in patients with Marfan syndrome remain limited, we compared the long-term outcomes after MV repair or replacement.

title: Left coronary ostial embolization by a migrated pledget after redo mitral valve replacement: a case report
authors: Tongkai Ge; Danjie Luo; Jimei Chen; Xiaofeng Li
abstract: Redo mitral valve replacement is associated with increased surgical complexity and perioperative risk. Acute coronary obstruction caused by retained surgical materials is extremely rare but can lead to fatal myocardial ischemia. A 64-year-old woman with prior bioprosthetic mitral valve replacement underwent redo surgery for severe intraprosthetic regurgitation. Shortly after separation from cardiopulmonary bypass, she developed ventricular fibrillation and severe myocardial dysfunction, requiring reinstitution of bypass and subsequent extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). Coronary angiography revealed a thrombus-like lesion at the left coronary ostium with preserved TIMI grade 3 flow; however, repeated aspiration failed to retrieve thrombotic material. Intravascular ultrasound demonstrated a solid non-thrombotic intraluminal obstruction. Surgical exploration confirmed complete occlusion of the left coronary ostium by a retained pledget from the previous operation. Removal of the pledget resulted in rapid improvement of myocardial contractility, and ECMO was successfully discontinued the following day. Coronary ostial embolization by retained pledget is a rare but life-threatening complication after redo mitral valve surgery. Early recognition, intravascular imaging, and timely surgical intervention with mechanical circulatory support are crucial for favorable outcomes.

title: Echoes of the past: Dressler syndrome presenting with haemorrhagic cardiac tamponade
authors: Horea‐Laurentiu Onea; Florin-Leontin Lazăr
abstract: Abstract Background Dressler syndrome (DS) is a rare immune-mediated pericarditis occurring after myocardial infarction (MI). Although typically associated with a mild pericardial effusion (PE), progression to cardiac tamponade is seldom encountered. Case summary We report a male patient in his 60s who developed DS 10 days after an extensive anterior MI. While on dual antiplatelet therapy and anticoagulation, he developed progressive PE, which, despite anti-inflammatory treatment and discontinuation of anticoagulants, failed to resolve. He subsequently experienced haemodynamic compromise and multiorgan failure, with echocardiographic signs of cardiac tamponade requiring urgent pericardiocentesis and evacuation of 600 mL of haemorrhagic fluid. The patient recovered uneventfully. Follow-up cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction, absence of viability in the infarct-related territory and no evidence of pericardial inflammation. Discussion This case highlights that DS, albeit rare in the reperfusion era, can still occur and may present with life-threatening haemorrhagic cardiac tamponade. In such cases, although still under debate, discontinuation of anticoagulation may be considered, underscoring the importance of vigilance and individualised management.

title: Echocardiographic findings in children with Sydenham chorea: a retrospective cross-sectional study
authors: Tesfaye Taye Gelaw; Habtamu Bayih Engida
abstract: In children with Sydenham chorea (SC), the prevalence of carditis (both clinical and subclinical carditis) is significant. Though SC often appears as an isolated manifestation, echocardiography frequently reveals valvular damage that goes undetected on auscultation. Determine the prevalence and patterns of clinical and subclinical carditis in children with Sydenham’s chorea at Tibebe-Ghion and Adinas General Hospitals. A retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of the archived echocardiographic findings of all children (aged 5–15) diagnosed with Sydenham chorea from June 2019 to March 2026 was done between July 8, 2026, and August 7, 2026. A multinomial logistic regression done using SPSS version 27 evaluated the associations between age, sex, and carditis status. Associations were reported as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals and significance at p < 0.05. Among 109 children with Sydenham chorea (mean age 10.07 ± 2.72 years; 59% female), 18% had no carditis, 66% had subclinical carditis, and 16% had clinical carditis. Mitral regurgitation (MR) was present in 82% of patients, primarily within the subclinical category (81%), with mild MR dominating subclinical cases (94%). Aortic regurgitation (AR) occurred in 22% of children, and 22% experienced combined MR and AR; isolated AR was not observed. Multinomial logistic regression demonstrated that neither age ( p = 0.929) nor sex ( p = 0.440) were significant predictors of carditis status. Echocardiography identified subclinical carditis in a substantial proportion of children with Sydenham chorea. These findings support the use of echocardiographic assessment in children with Sydenham chorea, particularly in high-burden settings. Not applicable.

title: Body Weight- and Age-Adjusted Reference Model for Septal Mitral Annular Plane Systolic Excursion in Healthy Dogs
abstract: Mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) is an M-mode index of left ventricular longitudinal systolic motion.In dogs, interpretation of raw MAPSE is affected by wide body size variation; and the independent effect of age after body weight adjustment has not been quantified.This study aimed to develop a body weight-and age-adjusted reference model for septal MAPSE and derive normalized indices.This two-center retrospective study included 180 client-owned healthy dogs examined between November 2016 and December 2023.Inclusion criteria included the absence of structural cardiac abnormalities, sinus rhythm, systolic blood pressure <140mmHg, and no clinically relevant thoracic radiographic, hematologic, or biochemical abnormalities.Septal MAPSE was measured by M-mode echocardiography from the apical four-chamber view and averaged over three cycles.Multiple linear regression modeled log₁₀(MAPSE), using log₁₀(body weight) and age.Heart rate and sex/neuter status were assessed as additional covariates, and study center was assessed for systematic center-related differences.Model-based Z-scores and percentage of predicted MAPSE values were calculated.The final model was log₁₀(MAPSE)=0.6279+0.3243×log₁₀(BW)-0.008767×age,explaining 70.2% of variation in log₁₀(MAPSE).Body weight and age were significant predictors (P<0.0001).Predicted MAPSE scaled allometrically with body weight and decreased by 2.0% per year.Z-scores and percentage of predicted MAPSE showed no residual association with body weight or age.Septal MAPSE in healthy dogs is body weightand age-dependent.This model provides body weight-and age-adjusted expected values for interpreting septal MAPSE within the range represented by this cohort.

title: Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure and severity of coronary artery lesions in patients with acute coronary syndrome: a retrospective observational cross-sectional analysis
authors: Caijie Dong; Lixiang Ma; Fu’e Zhang; Qi Qi; Wenli Kang; Zhian Jiang
abstract: Background Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease dominated by coronary atherosclerosis is the leading cause of global mortality and disability. Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is a well-established pathogenic driver, yet most existing studies rely on single cross-sectional LDL-C testing. Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure, calculated as a single fasting LDL-C measurement multiplied by age and serving as a proxy for lifelong lipid burden, remains insufficiently characterized regarding its association with coronary lesion severity. Methods This retrospective observational cross-sectional analysis enrolled 871 patients with acute coronary syndrome (ACS) undergoing coronary angiography between January and September 2024. Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure was calculated as fasting LDL-C measured within 24 h of admission (mmol/L) multiplied by age (years) and stratified into quartiles. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable screening. Multiple linear regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup interaction, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were performed to quantify associations and predictive performance. Results Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure was positively associated with the square root of the SYNTAX score ( β = 0.0098, P < 0.001). In covariate-adjusted ROC analyses, the model containing estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure showed slightly higher discrimination than the model containing age and LDL-C as separate additive terms (AUC 0.860 vs. 0.853; DeLong P = 0.0160), although the absolute difference was small (ΔAUC = 0.007). RCS analysis identified a nonlinear association ( P for nonlinearity = 0.026) with a point of maximum estimated slope at approximately 170.2 mmol·year/L; however, the 95% confidence interval was wide (56.6–177.9 mmol·year/L), and this value should not be interpreted as a validated threshold. Subgroup interaction tests revealed stronger associations in male patients and smokers (sex P = 0.036; smoking P = 0.047 both after FDR correction). Conclusions Estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure was independently associated with greater coronary lesion severity in patients with acute coronary syndrome. The estimated cumulative LDL-C exposure model showed modestly better fit and discrimination than the age + LDL-C model, although this finding should be interpreted cautiously because age is mathematically embedded in the exposure definition. These findings are consistent with the cumulative LDL-C exposure hypothesis and support its potential value in assessing coronary lesion burden.

title: Robotergestützte Herzchirurgie – eine aktuelle Übersichtsarbeit
authors: V. Rizzo; W. Crawford; V. Naruka; S. Mohammed; U. Kumar; K. Lall; S. Stamenkovich; B. Kyle; J. Edlin; Dincer Aktuerk
journal: Zeitschrift für Herz- Thorax- und Gefäßchirurgie
abstract: Zusammenfassung Hintergrund Die robotergestützte Herzchirurgie entwickelt sich von einer minimal invasiven Nischentechnik hin zu einer standardisierten Behandlungsoption. Den größten Nutzen bietet sie dabei in der Mitralklappenrekonstruktion sowie in ausgewählten Fällen der koronaren Revaskularisation. Zielsetzung und Methoden Narrative Übersichtsarbeit aktueller systematischer Übersichtsarbeiten, Register- und Datenbankstudien sowie Fallserien (aus Zentren mit hohen Patientenzahlen) zu robotergestützter Mitralklappenrekonstruktion, robotergestützter minimal invasiver direkter koronararterieller Bypassoperation (RA-MIDCAB), vollständig endoskopischer koronararterieller Bypassoperation (TECAB) und robotergestütztem Aortenklappenersatz, einschließlich Trainings- und Lernkurvendaten, um die gegenwärtigen Indikationen, den Nutzen für die Patienten, Hindernisse bei der Implementierung sowie Zukunftstrends zusammenzufassen. Ergebnisse Die robotergestützte Herzchirurgie (insbesondere mit dem da-Vinci-System) ermöglicht eine 3‑D-Visualisierung und die Verwendung abwinkelbarer Instrumente über kleine Ports, um das chirurgische Trauma zu senken. Die robotergestützte Mitralklappenrekonstruktion liefert gegenüber der Sternotomie und anderen minimal invasiven Verfahren trotz längerer Operationszeiten vergleichbare Ergebnisse in wichtigen Endpunkten, mit Vorteilen bei Schmerzen, Vorhofflimmern, Transfusionsbedarf und Aufenthaltsdauer. Die robotergestützte Koronarchirurgie (RA-MIDCAB/TECAB), zunehmend in Kombination mit einer perkutanen Koronarintervention im Rahmen hybrider Ansätze, ist in erfahrenen Zentren mit niedriger perioperativer Mortalität und Schlaganfallrate, sinkenden Konversionsraten und dauerhafter Bypass-Offenheitsrate assoziiert. Frühe Kohortendaten zum robotergestützten Aortenklappenersatz belegen Durchführbarkeit und kurze Aufenthaltsdauer, bei allerdings längerer Abklemmzeit/Dauer des kardiopulmonalen Bypasses. Die Verbreitung wird durch Kosten für Einrichtung und Verbrauchsmaterialien, Anforderungen an die Arbeitsabläufe und eine variable Lernkurve begrenzt. Proctoring-Programme (zur Beratung und Unterstützung), Simulationstraining und multidisziplinäre Teams in stabiler Zusammensetzung verbessern die Leistungsfähigkeit. Schlussfolgerung Die robotergestützte Herzchirurgie ist in spezialisierten Programmen sicher, reproduzierbar und förderlich hinsichtlich der Patientengenesung. Eine breitere Etablierung erfordert kosteneffektive Systeme, standardisierte Trainingskonzepte (einschließlich Simulation/telemedizinischer Mentoring-Programme), Langzeitdaten zu Haltbarkeit und Wert sowie anhaltende technische Innovationen.

title: Mapping and Outcome Implications of Left Atrial Low Voltage Regions as Determined by a Novel 122-electrode Spherical Mapping and Ablation Catheter
authors: Atul Verma; Hans Kottkamp; Hugh G Calkins; Devi G. Nair; Philipp Sommer; Ayman Ali Hussein; Burghard Schumacher; Srinivas Rao Dukkipati; Petr Neužil; Saumil R. Oza; Christopher E. Woods; Marc William Deyell; José Osorio; Vivek Yerrapu Reddy
abstract: Abstract Aims A novel 122-electrode spherical mapping/pulsed field ablation (PFA) device is known to effectively ablate atrial fibrillation (AF). The aim of this study is threshold optimization of LVA for the unique geometry of the Globe electrodes and the prognostic association, to evaluate if the extent of low voltage areas could predict recurrence. Methods and Results The PULSAR study was an IDE trial of 183 patients undergoing first-time paroxysmal AF ablation with one-year outcomes of any atrial arrhythmia. During this study, a subset of patients (n=82) had detailed pre-ablation voltage maps performed with the catheter. Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) was then performed with PFA. Patients were followed with weekly transtelephonic monitoring, ECG, and Holters at 3, 6, and 12 months. Recurrence was defined as any atrial arrhythmia (AA) > 30 seconds. Receiver operator curve (ROC) analysis revealed that a low voltage threshold of 1.0 mV had the highest value (0.735). The percentage LVA surface area resulting from a threshold of 1.0 mV that predicted AA recurrence was 11.6%. Univariate and multivariate analysis revealed the percentage LVA was the strongest predictor of AA recurrence. The 12-month freedom from AA was 84.6% and 52.9% for subjects under and over the low voltage area threshold respectively. Conclusions A voltage threshold of 1.0 mV is proposed as a threshold for defining LVA using the spherical catheter, but a range of approximately 0.5-1.5 mV yielded similar performance. Increased low voltage area in the pre-ablation atrial map was associated with a higher risk of AA recurrence.

title: MedDP : A Graph‐Based Large Language Disease Prediction Model
authors: Ran Wang; Guilin Qi
abstract: ABSTRACT Disease prediction from electronic health records (EHRs) is challenged by noisy clinical data, limited labelled data, and the lack of interpretable evidence supporting predictions. We propose MedDP, a graph‐based disease prediction framework that integrates large language models (LLMs) with structured diagnostic knowledge. MedDP extracts and normalises clinical entities from patient records restricted to information available before the prediction time, and constructs patient‐specific heterogeneous diagnostic graphs. A graph neural network encodes these graphs and retrieves candidate diseases, which are then assessed using LLM‐generated reasoning chains scored for semantic coherence and graph consistency. MedDP also incorporates pseudo‐label‐based self‐training to leverage unlabeled data in low‐resource settings. We evaluate MedDP on MIMIC‐III and DDXPlus. On MIMIC‐III, MedDP achieves an F1‐score of 0.6724 and an area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) of 0.812, outperforming the other baselines reported in the paper. On DDXPlus, it achieves an average F1‐score of 0.8163 across three diagnostic granularity levels. In few‐shot experiments on a 20,000‐patient MIMIC‐III subdataset, MedDP obtains an F1‐score of 0.512 using only 1% labelled data. These results indicate that combining graph‐based diagnostic representations with LLM reasoning can support disease prediction in the evaluated datasets and settings.

title: Advanced Hemodynamic Monitoring During Cesarean Section for Placenta Accreta Spectrum in a Pregnant Patient With Cardiac Disease and an Elevated BMI
authors: Georgia Ntalamagka; Giolanda Varvarousi; Emmanouil Stamatakis; Michail Pavlidis; Dimitrios Valsamidis
abstract: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) in parturients with significant cardiovascular disease presents major anesthetic and hemodynamic challenges, particularly when complicated by obesity and a high risk of hemorrhage.We report the successful perioperative management of a 42-year-old parturient at 35 weeks of gestation with repaired patent foramen ovale, hypertensive cardiomyopathy with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (40%), regional left ventricular wall motion abnormalities, moderate mitral regurgitation, obesity, and lumbar degenerative disc disease who underwent cesarean delivery under advanced hemodynamic monitoring.Regional anesthesia was selected over general anesthesia to minimize myocardial depression, sympathetic stimulation, and postoperative respiratory complications.A low-dose combined spinal-epidural technique was administered with gradual epidural extension to a T4 sensory level.Continuous invasive hemodynamic monitoring using the Hypotension Prediction Index (HPI; HemoSphere, 7.6 advanced monitoring platform from BD; software version 3.1) provided continuous assessment of cardiac output, stroke volume, systemic vascular resistance, dynamic arterial elastance, and left ventricular contractility (dP/dt).Norepinephrine was initiated immediately following intrathecal anesthesia and titrated to maintain arterial pressure and systemic vascular resistance close to baseline values, thereby minimizing the risk of neuraxial anesthesiainduced hypotension and potential myocardial hypoperfusion.The surgical procedure was complicated by dense pelvic adhesions, difficult bladder mobilization, and a prolonged skin-to-delivery interval of 12 minutes.Despite these challenges, hemodynamic stability was maintained throughout the procedure.Cardiac output increased from 5.5 L/min at baseline to 6.9 L/min following completion of epidural dosing, while stroke volume remained close to baseline.Although this change occurred temporally after completion of epidural dosing, a direct causal relationship could not be established from the available data.Following delivery, cardiac output decreased to 5.8 L/min without significant hemodynamic instability.Estimated blood loss was 1000 mL, and one unit of packed red blood cells was administered.Rotational thromboelastometry (ROTEM) analysis demonstrated preserved clot firmness and adequate fibrinogen contribution, with no evidence of clinically significant coagulopathy based on the available assessment.The neonate was delivered with an Apgar score of 8.This case highlights the potential value of combining carefully titrated neuraxial anesthesia with advanced hemodynamic monitoring in high-risk obstetric patients with cardiomyopathy and PAS.HPI-guided monitoring facilitated proactive vasopressor therapy and individualized hemodynamic management in a patient with limited cardiovascular reserve.Together, continuous hemodynamic assessment and point-ofcare ROTEM provided complementary information for cardiovascular and coagulation management.Further studies are needed to determine the role of HPI-guided management in parturients at high risk for hemorrhage and cardiovascular instability.

title: Maternally inherited PRKAR1A pathogenic variant causing Carney complex with a concomitant LDLR variant resulting in hyperlipidemia: a case report
authors: Caihong Guo; Hongwei Yi; Yujing Yang; Caiping Han; Qingkun Fan; Jie Wang; Chenggang Deng
abstract: Objective Carney complex (CNC) is an autosomal dominant multisystem tumor syndrome predominantly caused by pathogenic PRKAR1A mutations. Cardiac myxoma, multiple endocrine neoplasms and cutaneous pigmented lesions are its typical clinical manifestations. We report an extremely uncommon case of CNC caused by a PRKAR1A pathogenic variant, with a LDLR variant leading to familial hyperlipidemia and marked phenotypic heterogeneity within the family. Case presentation A 45-year-old male presented with palpitations was admitted to our hospital. The patient’s past medical history included cerebral infarction, myocardial infarction, right monocular blindness, and atrial myxoma. Physical examination revealed typical acromegalic facies, accompanied by markedly elevated serum growth hormone (GH) levels. Pituitary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) further identified a pituitary neuroendocrine tumor. Transthoracic echocardiography and contrast-enhanced cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) demonstrated global cardiac chamber enlargement and ventricular hypertrophy. Coronary CTA revealed diffuse dilatation of the coronary artery. Genetic testing confirmed two maternally inherited pathogenic variants: the splice-donor variant PRKAR1A c.769 + 1G>A responsible for CNC, and LDLR c.1879G>A, which causes familial hypercholesterolemia. One month after discharge from our hospital, the patient received transnasal transsphenoidal resection of sellar pituitary lesion under general anesthesia at the Department of Neurosurgery in another general hospital. Preoperative GH and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) were elevated on repeat testing, and both decreased significantly postoperatively. The sellar lesion was confirmed as a plurihormonal pituitary neuroendocrine tumor of pituitary transcription factor 1 (PIT-1) lineage; immunohistochemistry showed weak GH expression, focal prolactin (PRL) and luteinizing hormone (LH) expression, negative adrenocorticotropic hormone(ACTH) and T-box pituitary transcription factor(T-PIT) staining, with a Ki-67 labeling index of ~1%. Conclusion The splice-site variant PRKAR1A c.769 + 1G>A represents a well-documented recurrent pathogenic variant among patients with CNC. The majority of previously reported carriers develop primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease (PPNAD) and overt Cushing syndrome. However, our patient presented with acromegaly driven by a plurihormonal PIT-1-lineage pituitary neuroendocrine tumor without corticotroph differentiation. accompanied by atrial myxoma, cardiac hypertrophy, cardiomegaly, coronary dilatation, and familial hypercholesterolemia secondary to an LDLR mutation. This rare coexisting genetic phenotype underscores the value of prompt genetic and endocrine screening for at-risk patients.

title: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
authors: Manisha Singh; Keegan Mendez; Brian C. Ayers; Sophie X. Wang; Atsushi Takahashi; Debbie Lin Teodorescu; Jordi Mill; Carlos Albors; Andreas Escher; Yiling Fan; Çağlar Öztürk; Eve Sheridan; Emma Rutherford; Oscar Camara; Tarun Chakravarty; Ellen Tunney Roche
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) poses significant clinical challenges due to the complex and variable geometry of the left atrial appendage (LAA), whose structure complicates the development of personalized interventions like LAA occlusion (LAAO) for stroke prevention Current reliance on animal models and cadavers for the assessment of left atrium (LA) and LAA to study AF-related disease and interventions raises reproducibility concerns, necessitating the development of high fidelity, physiologically relevant tools. To address this, we present a multimodal framework combining a soft robotic benchtop simulator, a lumped parameter model (LPM), and finite element analysis (FEA) to replicate LA function in sinus rhythm, atrial flutter, and AF. The system integrates 3D-printed, patient-specific LA geometries with soft robotic actuators to reproduce realistic wall motion and hemodynamics. A compact, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-compatible flow loop, driven by a soft robotic left ventricle (LV), eliminates bulky and non-physiological pulsatile pumps, allowing precise flow measurements and LAAO device testing under clinically relevant conditions. Complementary LPM and FEA models provide mechanistic insights, quantifying systemic hemodynamic changes and LA wall stress during disease and interventions. The models effectively replicate the clinical markers of atrial dysfunction and arrhythmia disorders, and their physiological accuracy is demonstrated through validation against human imaging and porcine models. The soft robotic LV's ability to drive the mock flow loop is validated in a hybrid synthetic-biological configuration within a swine circulatory system, where the soft robotic ventricle replaces native ventricular contraction to sustain systemic circulation. This scalable and versatile framework integrates experimental and computational techniques to advance cardiovascular biomechanics, supporting device development, clinical research/training, and personalized AF treatment to improve patient outcomes.

title: Exercise-Induced Tricuspid Regurgitation
authors: Claudia Baratto; Mattia Mercurio; Denisa Muraru; Francesca Heilbron; Michele Tomaselli; Giovanni Battista Perego; Fabio Previdi; Stefano Paleari; Luigi Fiocca; Michele Senni; Jean‐Luc Vachiéry; Vishal N. Rao; Ryan James Tedford; Marat Fudim; Gianfranco Parati; Luigi Paolo Badano; Sergio Caravita
abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise-induced preload/afterload changes could affect tricuspid regurgitation (TR). OBJECTIVES: The study aims to assess exercise-induced TR (exTR+), its consequences, and predictors. METHODS: Consecutive patients underwent exercise cardiac catheterization and three-dimensional echocardiography. ExTR+ was defined as a ≥1 grade increase in TR severity. RESULTS: ExTR+ occurred in 34% of 132 patients. Patients with exTR+ were older, had more atrial fibrillation, higher natriuretic peptides/heart failure with preserved ejection fraction probability scores, higher filling pressures, and lower cardiac output (P < 0.05). ExTR+ displayed greater right ventricular dilation, right atrial pressure rise, lower cardiac output, and lower oxygen consumption (P < 0.05). Exercise rather than resting TR regurgitant volume was more associated with cardiac output and oxygen consumption. Baseline TR, atrial fibrillation, and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide (OR: 1.065, 4.97, and 1.0004 per pg/mL, respectively, P < 0.05) predicted exTR+ (area under the curve: 0.91). CONCLUSIONS: ExTR+ is frequent, identifies heart failure with preserved ejection fraction-like phenotypes with a maladaptive exercise response, and adds information beyond resting TR.

title: The impact of maternal cardiovascular risk factors and diseases on offspring cardiovascular health
authors: Alexandr Ceasovschih; Sura Markos; Stanislav Nikolaevich Kotlyarov; Victorița Șorodoc; Maciej Banach
abstract: The increasing number of pregnancies among women at cardiovascular risk or with established cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) has become a major global health concern because of its lasting influence on the health of their offspring. Maternal heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, obesity, and abnormal lipid levels, including also elevated lipoprotein(a), can disturb fetal growth and development, leading to changes in the heart, blood vessels, and metabolism that raise the risk of CVD problems in childhood and later life. The rising age of pregnant women, especially in the developed countries, also increases this risk. These effects result from a combination of inherited traits and alterations in the intrauterine environment, including impaired blood flow, inflammation, oxidative stress, and disrupted nutrient transfer through the placenta. Such disturbances can modify the structure and function of the developing cardiovascular system and contribute to lifelong vulnerability to CVDs. Studies from large populations show that children born to mothers with cardiovascular conditions have about twice the risk of developing CVD compared with those born to healthy mothers. Good maternal health before and during pregnancy, supported by balanced nutrition, regular physical activity, and effective control of blood pressure, lipids, body weight, and blood sugar, is strongly linked to better outcomes for both mother and child. Although current lifestyle interventions in pregnancy have shown promising effects on maternal wellbeing, their influence on the long-term cardiovascular health of the offspring remains uncertain. Strengthening preconception care, well-designed healthcare education, improving cardiovascular screening in women of reproductive age, and promoting heart-healthy habits across the life course are essential to prevent the transfer of cardiovascular risk from one generation to the next.

title: Decreasing Births and NICU Admissions for Congenital Anomalies in the United States, 2016-2023
authors: Krishna Acharya; DonnaMaria E. Cortezzo; Erin L. Rholl; Jessica T. Fry; Stefanie L. Riddle; Erwin Cabacungan
abstract: Abstract Objectives: Evaluate trends in U.S. births and NICU admissions for congenital anomalies Study Design: This population-based, cross-sectional study included all births with congenital anomalies in the U.S. from 2016 to 2023 from CDC WONDER. Trends in anomaly-associated NICU admissions and births were assessed. Results: From 2016-2023, NICU admissions for anomalies decreased from 18.5 to 18 per 10,000 live births (annual percent change (APC), -0.4%; 95% CI, -0.7% to -0.2%). Admissions for gastroschisis showed the greatest decline; admissions for cyanotic congenital heart disease (CCHD) increased. NICU trends approximated birth trends for neonatal surgical anomalies, and not for non-surgical or life-limiting anomalies. Conclusions: Births and NICU admissions for congenital anomalies declined modestly in the U.S. from 2016 to 2023 with births decreasing to a greater degree than NICU admissions. Anomaly-specific considerations such as need for neonatal surgical repair, comorbid diagnoses requiring NICU care, and parental goals of care may explain these differences.
