title: Desenlaces cardiovasculares y de seguridad de los iSGLT2 en pacientes con falla cardíaca que se encuentran en diálisis
authors: María Antonia Mesa‐Maya; Juan José Hurtado-Guerra; Tomás Echavarría-Bayter; María J. Baena-Duque; Valeria López-Cardona; Elsa M. Vásquez-Trespalacios; Néstor A. López-Pompey; Laura Duque-González
abstract: Introducción: La falla cardíaca es una complicación relevante en pacientes con enfermedad renal crónica avanzada.Los inhibidores del cotransportador sodio-glucosa tipo 2 (iSGLT2) han mostrado beneficios en la función renal y eventos cardiovasculares en esta población, pero su uso en diálisis sigue siendo poco estudiado.Objetivo: Evaluar el efecto de los iSGLT2 en pacientes con falla cardíaca en diálisis, analizando su impacto en la fracción de eyección del ventrículo izquierdo (FEVI), la clase funcional NYHA, la hospitalización y la mortalidad.Métodos: Estudio de cohorte retrospectiva en pacientes con falla cardíaca en diálisis en un hospital colombiano.Se incluyeron 15 pacientes; 13 completaron el seguimiento, uno falleció y otro se perdió durante el periodo de estudio.Resultados: Se observó un aumento medio de 12.99 puntos porcentuales en la FEVI, pasando de 37.9% a 51.0%.Al ingreso, 66.7% tenían FEVI ≤ 40%; al seguimiento, el 100% recuperó una FEVI > 40%.También se registró una reducción de peso promedio de 1.68 kg.Hubo una muerte (6.7%) y dos hospitalizaciones, sin eventos adversos graves asociados.Conclusiones: El uso de iSGLT2 en pacientes con falla cardíaca en diálisis mostró tendencia a mejorar la función cardíaca sin aumentar eventos adversos.Se requieren estudios más amplios para confirmar estos hallazgos.

title: Proventricular dilation disease in Psittaciformes: a retrospective study of cases received in four diagnostic laboratories in California, USA, 2014–2024
authors: Jeann Leal de Araújo; Mauricio A. Navarro; Francisco Alejandro Uzal; Hernando Daniel Acevedo; Jennine Ochoa; Emma H. Torii; R. Reséndiz; Akinyi C. Nyaoke; Carmen F. Jerry; Simone T. Stoute; Javier Asín
abstract: Introduction Proventricular dilation disease (PDD), caused by parrot bornaviruses (PaBVs), is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in captive psittacines worldwide. However, comprehensive retrospective studies evaluating its clinicopathologic spectrum remain scarce. This study aimed to characterize the epidemiologic, clinical, gross, microscopic, and concurrent disease findings of naturally occurring PDD in psittacine birds. Methods A retrospective study was conducted using necropsy records of Psittaciformes submitted to four veterinary diagnostic laboratories in California, USA, between 2014 and 2024. Cases were included based on compatible lesions and immunohistochemical detection of PaBV antigen. Clinical signs, gross and microscopic lesions, concurrent diseases, and differences between psittacine superfamilies were evaluated. Results Of 1,466 Psittaciformes necropsies, 51 cases met the inclusion criteria. Gastrointestinal signs alone predominated (59%), followed by combined gastrointestinal and neurologic signs (14%) and neurologic signs alone (12%). Death without previously reported clinical signs occurred in 12% of birds. Gross gastrointestinal dilation was observed in 70% of cases, whereas 30% lacked specific gross lesions. Histologically, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrates most frequently involved the gizzard (86%), proventriculus (73%), adrenal glands (72%), brain (71%), and heart (49%). Concurrent diseases were identified in 57% of cases. PDD was diagnosed significantly more frequently in Cacatuoidea than in Psittacoidea (9/98 [9.2%] versus 42/1,304 [3.2%]; p = 0.007), although clinical signs and lesions did not differ significantly between superfamilies. Discussion These findings highlight the broad clinicopathologic spectrum of naturally occurring PDD, including cases without characteristic gross lesions or previously reported clinical signs. The frequent involvement of gastrointestinal and nervous tissues underscores the importance of comprehensive tissue sampling and histologic examination for an accurate diagnosis.

title: Medical Preconditioning in Infants and Young Children with Secundum Atrial Septal Defect: Effects of Preload and Afterload Reduction on Defect Size and Right Ventricular Remodeling
authors: Mahmoud Othman; Osama Abdelaziz; Ahmed Mossa; Ahmed Gamal; Ayman Gobara; Hayat Nassar; Ashraf Harashash; Hala Mounir Agha
abstract: Abstract Objectives: To evaluate the effects of preload reduction using furosemide and combined preload–afterload reduction therapy using furosemide plus captopril on atrial septal defect (ASD) secundum size, right ventricular (RV) dimensions, and cardiac remodeling in infants and young children over a one-year follow-up period. Patients & Methods: This prospective, non-randomized controlled study included 90 infants and young children with isolated secundum ASD. Patients were allocated into three equal groups: Group I receivedf urosemide, Group II received furosemide plus captopril, and Group III served as untreated controls. Clinical, anthropometric, and echocardiographic assessments were performed at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. Primary outcomes were changes in ASD diameter and RV size. Secondary outcomes included left ventricular ejection fraction (EF), fractional shortening (FS), tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (TAPSE), TAPSE Z-score, and TAPSE/ESPAP ratio. Statistical analysis included ANOVA, Kruskal–Wallis, paired tests, and post hoc comparisons Results: Baseline characteristics were comparable among the three groups. After 12 months, ASD size differed significantly between groups (P < 0.001). The mean reduction in ASD size from baseline to one year was greatest in Group II (3.4 ± 5.5 mm), followed by Group I (1.31 ± 4.3 mm), whereas Group III showed minimal change (0.32 ± 2.5 mm; P = 0.004). Post hoc analysis demonstrated significant differences between Group II and Group III (P = 0.001) and between Group I and Group III, while the difference between Groups I and II showed a trend toward significance (P = 0.05). RV diameter decreased significantly in both treated groups at 6 and 12 months (P < 0.001) but remained persistently dilated in untreated controls. EF showed a mild but statistically significant improvement in treated groups compared with controls. TAPSE and TAPSE Z-scores improved significantly over time in all groups, with no significant intergroup differences. Conclusion: .The use of furosemide, alone or with captopril, significantly were associated with ASD size reduction and favorable right ventricular remodeling in infants and young children with secundum ASD, providing effective medical bridging strategy to transcatheter closure.

title: Infected Pancreatic Walled-off Necrosis Following Hypertriglyceridemia-Induced Necrotizing Pancreatitis: A Case Report
authors: Daniel Odio Cortés; Kevin Cruz Mora; Jeaustin Mora-Jiménez; Esteban Zavaleta‐Monestel
abstract: Infected walled-off necrosis (WON) is a serious complication of necrotizing pancreatitis that requires timely, evidence-based management.We describe the case of a 41-year-old man with a history of severe hypertriglyceridemia-associated necrotizing pancreatitis who presented with an encapsulated pancreatic/peripancreatic collection containing intralesional gas, consistent with infected WON.Contrastenhanced computed tomography showed no evidence of new pancreatic parenchymal necrosis, and the available findings did not establish a recurrent episode of acute necrotizing pancreatitis.The patient underwent endoscopic ultrasound-guided transmural drainage followed by two endoscopic necrosectomies as part of a step-up approach, combined with antimicrobial therapy.Cultures obtained from the necrotic collection identified uncommon microorganisms, including Rothia mucilaginosa, Solobacterium moorei, and Peptostreptococcus anaerobius.During an endoscopic procedure, the patient developed narrow-complex tachycardia with transient hypotension.Subsequent electrocardiographic evaluation revealed ventricular pre-excitation consistent with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, although the mechanism of the acute arrhythmia could not be definitively established.Following multidisciplinary management, the patient demonstrated favorable clinical improvement during hospitalization and was discharged.This case highlights the role of minimally invasive step-up management in appropriately selected patients, the importance of interpreting unusual microbiological findings in their clinical context, and the need to recognize cardiovascular conditions that may influence procedural safety.Further investigation is warranted to clarify the clinical significance of uncommon microorganisms isolated from infected WON.

title: Female Fingerprint: Sex-Specific Aspects in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and Heart Failure
authors: Esther Roth; Laura Rottner
abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and heart failure (HF) frequently coexist and represent a major source of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This review summarizes current evidence on sex-specific differences in epidemiology, pathophysiology, clinical presentation, prognosis, and treatment in women with AF and HF. RECENT FINDINGS: Emerging evidence indicates that women with AF and HF constitute a distinct clinical and biological phenotype. Women typically develop AF at older age, more commonly present with hypertension and HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and report greater symptom burden and impaired quality of life. Sex-specific mechanisms including hormonal influences, atrial fibrosis, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, and microvascular disease contribute to these differences. Population studies further demonstrate sex-related disparities in HF development and outcomes across AF subtypes. Despite increasing awareness, women remain underrepresented in clinical trials and are less likely to receive rhythm-control strategies, catheter ablation, or device therapy. Recognition of the "female fingerprint" in AF and HF is essential for individualized risk stratification and the advancement of precision cardiovascular medicine.

title: Multimodality noninvasive imaging in the evaluation of coronary artery disease: a narrative review
authors: Karim Hoyek; Anthony Bedran; Elio Haroun; Joseph Hajj; Ziad Zalaquett; Ankit Agrawal; Daniella Aro Arockiam; Clement Tan; Tom Kai Ming Wang
abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, and its evaluation has evolved beyond the identification of obstructive epicardial stenosis alone. Contemporary imaging increasingly emphasizes an integrated assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque burden and composition, lesion-specific ischemia, myocardial viability, scar, ventricular remodeling, and coronary microvascular dysfunction. Anatomic and functional imaging provide complementary information regarding coronary atherosclerosis, lesion-specific physiology, inducible ischemia, myocardial blood flow, viability, scar, and microvascular disease, with test selection guided by the clinical question and patient characteristics. Randomized trials of specific imaging-guided strategies have demonstrated differences in diagnostic efficiency, downstream invasive angiography, preventive therapy, revascularization, and procedural complications. In contrast, effects on symptoms and hard cardiovascular outcomes vary according to the population, comparator, and duration of follow-up. Emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, radiomics, photon-counting computed tomography, molecular imaging, and hybrid imaging, are at different stages of clinical readiness and require varying degrees of further validation before routine implementation. This review summarizes the current role, evidence base, limitations, and future directions of multimodality noninvasive imaging in CAD, providing a practical framework for selecting the appropriate test according to the clinical question and patient profile.

title: Functional health literacy and medication adherence in atrial fibrillation patients
authors: Parisa Janjani; Alireza Haraj; Parisa Nosrati; Vesal Hasani; Pejman Ardalan; Saba Hasani; Setayesh Moradinia; Mohammad Mahdi Khodaie; Mobin Dorost; Sahar Dehpahlevan; Majid Haghjoo; Parand Shariat Rad
journal: American Heart Journal Plus Cardiology Research and Practice
abstract: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) treatment requires strict, long-term adherence to oral anticoagulants (OACs) to decrease associated morbidity risks. Despite its importance, adherence varies widely; nonadherence contributes to life-threatening adverse outcomes and elevated costs. Health literacy (HL)—the ability to acquire, comprehend, evaluate, and apply health information—is an important, yet underestimated factor. Given conflicting evidence on the HL-adherence association in chronic diseases, this study investigated this relationship and influencing demographic/contextual factors in AF patients across Iran. Methods This descriptive-analytical cross-sectional, multicenter study was conducted in 2025 across Tehran, Kurdistan, and Kermanshah provinces on 407 adult AF patients receiving OAC therapy. Functional HL was assessed using the HELIA questionnaire; medication adherence was evaluated via MMAS-8. Analysis involved Pearson correlation, independent-samples t -tests, and multiple linear regression. Results Mean total HL score was 108.65 ± 30.96 (moderate); mean MMAS-8 was 2.61 ± 1.54 (relatively high adherence). Total HL demonstrated a significant negative correlation with MMAS-8 scores (r = −0.099, p < 0.05), indicating higher HL associates with improved adherence, driven primarily by the “Information” subscale (r = −0.172, p < 0.01). While males had significantly higher HL scores (p < 0.001), females showed better adherence (p = 0.045). Notably, older age was paradoxically linked to worse adherence in Kurdistan (r = 0.327, p < 0.01). In multiple linear regression adjusting for age, gender, and study site (R 2 = 0.214, p < 0.001), total HL emerged as a strong independent predictor of better adherence (β = −0.500, p < 0.001), alongside older age, female gender, and residing in Kurdistan (all p < 0.001). Conclusions Health literacy is a statistically significant, independent and modifiable predictor of medication adherence in Iranian AF populations. Efficacy is specific to functional information application, highlighting the need for interventions focused on practical skills. The complex age-gender interaction demonstrates how regional socioeconomic and cultural contexts affect the HL-adherence relationship.

title: Serum creatinine- and cystatin C-derived sarcopenia-related indices and the risk of all-cause mortality in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation
authors: Yu Wang; Guipeng An; Xiangjuan Liu; Lianyue Ma; Xiao Meng; Huixia Lu; Mei Dong
abstract: Background Sarcopenia is increasingly recognized as an important predictor of adverse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). However, the prognostic relevance of sarcopenia-related indices derived from serum creatinine and cystatin C in patients undergoing TAVI has not been fully established. Methods This prospective study included 465 patients who underwent TAVI for symptomatic aortic stenosis. Associations between sarcopenia-related indices and all-cause mortality were assessed using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis, Cox proportional hazards models, and restricted cubic spline analysis (RCS). Predictive performance and incremental prognostic value were compared across indices using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves (ROC), the Harrell’s C-index, net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed to examine the robustness of the findings. Results During a median follow-up of 2.8 years, 59 (12.7%) deaths occurred. In the fully adjusted Cox model, each 1-standard deviation increase in eGFRcys/eGFRcr (HR 0.29, 95% CI 0.11–0.75; p = 0.011) and Cr * eGFRcys (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.14–0.64; p = 0.002) was associated with a lower risk of all-cause mortality. Time-dependent ROC indicated that Cr * eGFRcys had the most favorable predictive performance among the evaluated indices. Adding Cr * eGFRcys to the fully adjusted model increased the concordance index from 0.696 to 0.736 and significantly improved risk reclassification and discrimination (NRI: 0.437, 95% CI 0.171–0.704, p = 0.001; IDI: 0.026, 95% CI 0.004–0.048, p = 0.022). Findings from subgroup and sensitivity analyses were broadly consistent. Conclusion Among patients with symptomatic aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI, lower eGFRcys/eGFRcr and Cr * eGFRcys were associated with a higher risk of all-cause mortality after the procedure. Notably, Cr * eGFRcys showed stronger prognostic value and may provide additional prognostic information for risk stratification in patients undergoing TAVI.

title: A Lobar Hematoma Mimicking a Brain Tumor in a Patient With Two Mechanical Heart Valves: The Value of Serial Magnetic Resonance Imaging
authors: Clara Pinto; Alexandre Castro Lopes; Ana Sofia Pimenta; Carolina M Marçal; Ana S Martins
abstract: Subacute intracerebral hemorrhage can resemble a neoplasm on imaging, particularly when it is heterogeneous, surrounded by edema, and lacks a typical hyperacute appearance.We describe the case of a 76-year-old woman with mechanical aortic and mitral prostheses on warfarin who presented with right hemiparesis and an international normalized ratio (INR) of 4.5.Brain computed tomography showed a 2.3 cm heterogeneous left frontal parasagittal lesion with surrounding edema, without contrast enhancement.Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed a 24 × 23 × 15 mm lesion with peripheral T1 hyperintensity, a cystic/necrotic center, marked susceptibility artifact, and finger-like perilesional edema, along with scattered cerebral and cerebellar microbleeds.Primary or metastatic tumor, infection, septic embolism from prosthetic endocarditis, and cerebral amyloid angiopathy were considered.Thoraco-abdominopelvic computed tomography, infectious serologies, blood cultures, and transesophageal echocardiography did not support neoplastic or infectious causes.Serial MRI at six weeks showed near-complete resolution of edema with signal changes typical of late subacute blood products, and at seven months, a small residual hemosiderin-lined cavity without mass effect.The patient recovered independent gait.After a complete systemic workup and neurosurgical referral, serial MRI showing the expected evolution of blood products established the diagnosis before a biopsy was required, which was particularly relevant in a patient at high thrombotic and bleeding risk.
